河西边塞屯戍吏卒们因事、因病、因丧皆可按程序请假。河西边塞有一套严格的请假制度。一般情况下，由请假者先向本部门官长请假，本部门再上报上一级，由上级批复准予。从居延汉简的记载可知，居延地区屯戍吏卒常患的疾病主要是伤寒、寒热、伤汗、温、肠澼等。
en:
Unearthed in 1974 at the Jiaqu Houguan Site, this bamboo slip is a formal request for sick leave. It was filed by Dang, a minor frontier government official suffering from chest tightness, severe bloating, and a complete loss of appetite, leaving him too weak to work. Two days later, his superior, a Watchtower Commander named Kuang, forwarded the report to the Juyan Commandant's Office, formally requesting permission for Dang to leave his post and see a doctor.
This artifact offers a fascinating glimpse into the strict bureaucracy of the Hexi Frontier garrisons. Officers and soldiers had to follow a rigid chain of command to request time off for personal matters, illness, or mourning. Furthermore, Juyan Han bamboo slips reveal the harsh realities of frontier life, showing that the most common ailments among the guards were typhoid, severe chills, heatstroke, and dysentery.

然则这岂非人生一趣吗？抱歉，又要说抱歉了，因为我仍要去赴这一场约战。
我实在喜欢练剑，像攀一座没有尽头的山。武道的绝顶究竟在何处，从无人知晓。
可它就是在那里。如今我要去攀了。或死，或赢，皆未可知。
但我定是欢喜的——能这样去试一试，去做那天下第一。
待我战罢，便来寻你，好么？两年四十二天了，现在你会同我说话了吧？

en:
To Yao, my best friend.
Please, don't be angry with me. You were right. Just as you've always been, all these years. It seems I always have to hit a wall before I'm willing to turn back.
But isn't that one of the joys of life? Forgive me. I have to say "forgive me" again... because I'm still going to that duel.
Learning the blade is like climbing a mountain with no summit. No one has ever known where the pinnacle of martial arts lies.
It's out there, though. And I will climb to it. In victory, or defeat... Who can say.
But I am happy. I have the chance to become the Greatest Under Heaven.
Once I'm done... I'll find you, alright? It's been two years and forty-two days. You'll finally talk to me now, won't you?
If you still don't want to... Then... would you like some fish?

zh: 王十三是家中第十三个孩子，上头有十二个哥哥姐姐。母亲生她时落下了病根，没几年便撒手人寰。父亲为了养活家中的孩子，又常年在外做工。她便是被她这些哥哥姐姐们拉扯长大的。但她从不是个柔弱受保护的妹妹。正相反，打她懂事起，她便像个小大人一样，操持起整个家庭。与她那些老实的哥哥姐姐不同，王十三生就一双锐眼，又跟着哥哥姐姐到处讨生活，养就了一颗七窍玲珑心。她见人说人话，见鬼说鬼话，游走市井间，像条滑溜的胖头鱼。经她劝说，王家的孩子们进城做起了生意，且在她的操作下，王家的生意越做越大。但是，却碍了地头蛇的眼。他们这些人啊，在江州李家眼里，那不过是可以随意踩踏的蝼蚁。不过一夜时间，王家铺子全被烧毁，王十三的哥哥姐姐们为了保护王十三，全死于那场大火中。王十三在大火中幸存下来，几乎是爬着进了开封。她想要成为人上人。唯有手握权势，方能去报这滔天大仇……但她又不知道从何做起。
en: Wang Shisan is the thirteenth child in her family, born into a home already bursting with siblings. Her mother fell gravely ill after delivering her and soon passed away. Her father, constantly away working to keep the household afloat, leaves the child to be raised by her elder brothers and sisters. But Wang Shisan is never the delicate, coddled youngest. From the moment she could speak and understand the world around her, she stepped into the role of household manager. Unlike her honest, straightforward siblings, she has sharp eyes and a mind. Trailing behind her siblings as they scraped together a living, she learns to read people and situations and navigates the world with uncanny savvy. Slick as an eel and quick with words, she built connections, won favors, and convinced her siblings to start a small business in the city. Under her clever management, it thrived. But their rising fortune soon drew attention from the local hoodlums. To the Li family of Jiangzhou, the Wangs are nothing more than pawns to be swept aside. One night, without warning, the family's shop was burned down. All her siblings perished, trying to shield her from the flames. Wang Shisan crawled out of the wreckage alone, making her way to Kaifeng with nothing but vengeance in her heart. She knew she had to grasp power because only then could she make the Li family pay for what they'd done. But she had no idea where to begin.

zh:
泰山道上从此多了三个挑山工。
老人叫“山大”，是三兄弟的本家，山夫管他叫“师父”，三个弟弟也跟着他叫。
师父话少，教得也少。第一天，他扔给三兄弟一人一根扁担，就说了一个字：“挑。”
他们挑的是石头，从山脚到山腰，从山腰到山顶，再从山顶下来。师父往石头上涂了一层红粉，说要跑三个来回，粉不掉，才算火候到。
山夫不明白，只是埋头学。手臂酸得抬不起来，膝盖肿得像桃子，也要继续学。老二问他疼不疼，山夫说不疼。老三说俺疼，山夫说那也忍着。
师父一边在山脚下挑登山客，一边看着他们一趟趟下来，沉默得像石头。
山夫问过一回：“师父，你以前也是闯江湖的么？”
师父没答，山夫便不再问了。
一年后，师父开始让他们挑人。
头一回挑的是个去文津馆访学的老秀才。老秀才瘦得像根柴，山夫担起来，却觉得他比石头还沉。
人是不一样的，人是活的，会动，会说话，会怕。石头磨掉了一层粉，也不会痛；人若是磨掉了一层皮，便是受伤。
“别怕，俺手艺好着呢！”山夫说。
他学着师父的模样，呼喝一声，双臂发力，老秀才便到了半山腰。他弟弟山天在那儿，还能再送老秀才一程。
泰山每年每月都有许多人来，去文津馆的书生，去早悟寺的香客，逃难投亲的妇人，告老还乡的官。
每个人来请他挑，都把命交给了他。命这个东西，比石头沉多了。
山夫越挑越稳，有时闲下来，也听登山客们说各自的故事。有妇人的丈夫被契丹掳了去，再没回来；有老人的儿子死在黄河边上，尸骨无存。
他们不约而同来到泰山，泰山上有保佑他们的碧霞元君，泰山后是富饶安定的青州。
近来山夫总是想起多年前的那个夜晚。破庙，两个人，刀光一闪，死这件事简单得像切菜。
那是他头一回见到死，也是最后一回。后来他们在山路上来来回回，再没见过悬赏令，没见过刀光，没见过一个人说死就死。
老三问他：“哥，这算不算江湖？”
十八岁那年，山夫对着破庙里的神像磕头，那时他觉得江湖是杀出来的，是刀尖上滚出来的。现在他却觉得，江湖可以是挑出来的。
他对老三说：“算。”
他顿了顿，又说：“江湖不是俺们想的那样。这，就是江湖。”
en:
Mount Tai soon had three new porters walking its steep trails.
The old man's name was Shan Da. Since they shared the same family name, Shan Fu simply called him "Master," and his brothers quickly followed suit.
The old man was a man of few words, and he taught them even less. On their very first day, he tossed each of them a wooden carrying pole and grunted a single instruction: "Carry."
So, they carried rocks. Up from the base of the mountain to the halfway mark, up to the peak, and all the way back down. The Master dusted their boulders with red powder, warning them that their technique wouldn't be passable until they could make three full round trips without rubbing off a single speck.
Shan Fu didn't see the point, but he kept his head down and worked. Even when his arms burned too much to lift and his knees swelled up like melons, he pushed through. When his middle brother asked if it hurt, Shan Fu lied and said no. When the youngest whined about the agony, Shan Fu just told him to grit his teeth and bear it.
Meanwhile, the Master went right on hauling tourists up from the base. He watched the brothers trudge up and down the steps, as silent and unmoving as a stone himself.
Shan Fu only pried once. "Master, did you use to roam the jianghu, too?"
When the old man offered no answer, Shan Fu let it drop forever.
It took a full year before the Master finally let them carry actual people.
Shan Fu's first passenger was a frail old scholar heading up to the Inkbound Order. The man was nothing but skin and bones, yet when Shan Fu hoisted the pole onto his shoulders, the scholar somehow felt heavier than the boulders ever had.
People were different. People were alive. They shifted, they breathed, and they got scared. If a rock bumped into something and lost its powder, it didn't feel a thing. If a person scraped against a cliff face, they bled.
"Don't worry, I've got steady hands!" Shan Fu called out, trying to reassure him.
Mimicking the Master, he let out a sharp grunt, drove power through his legs, and hauled the scholar all the way to the halfway point, where his brother was waiting to take the passenger the rest of the way.
Month after month, year after year, Mount Tai saw an endless stream of visitors: scholars bound for the Inkbound Order, pilgrims climbing to Seedling Temple, refugees fleeing to family, and tired officials retiring to their hometowns.
Every single person who paid for a ride was putting their life in his hands. And a human life weighed a hell of a lot more than a stone.
Shan Fu's footing only grew steadier with time. In his rare moments of rest, he would listen to the mountain climbers' stories. One woman wept for a husband dragged off by Khitan raiders, never to be seen again. An old man mourned a son who died on the banks of the Yellow River, his bones lost to the mud.
They all came to Mount Tai for a reason. At the summit sat the Lady Bixia, who might just answer their prayers. And beyond the mountain lay the safe, prosperous lands of Qingzhou.
Lately, Shan Fu found his mind drifting back to that pitch-black night years ago. The ruined temple, the two men, the sudden flash of steel. How easily a life could be snuffed out, as casual as chopping vegetables.
That was the first time he'd ever looked death in the face, and it was the last. Walking up and down these ancient steps, he never saw another bounty token, never saw a blade drawn in anger, and never watched a man die on a whim.
"Brother," the youngest asked him one day, wiping sweat from his brow. "Does this count as being in the jianghu?"
Back when he was eighteen, bowing to a faceless god in a ruined shrine, Shan Fu had fully believed the jianghu was a legend carved out by killing, a life lived strictly on the edge of a blade. But now, he understood that the jianghu could just as easily be carried on a man's shoulders.
He looked at his brother. "It does."
He paused, looking out over the endless mountain steps. "It's just not what we thought it was. This is the jianghu."

zh:
有一日，大葱路过涌泉镇，看见一位游侠在岸边垂钓。
游侠背把旧剑，鱼篓空空。钓累了，便收竿拎着空篓转身，一眼瞧见大葱，便伸手来摸。
大葱它是有身份的文明猫子，按说早就脱离了本性，可它鬼使神差地翻倒，四脚朝天，露出软肚皮喵喵喵，等着游侠像旁人一样好猫乖猫地一通乱叫。
游侠没叫，游侠说我也有只猫！它已经是我的好猫啦。
骗猫！你的猫在哪呢？
大葱想走，可它没有走。大葱蹲在游侠身边，尾巴搭在游侠袖口。一人一猫，从黄昏坐到星起。
游侠起身时，大葱跟了上去。游侠问，你要跟我走？大葱脚步端庄没有回答。
真叫猫操心啊！往常大葱只知道小猫们需要文明猫的帮助，没想到人也需要文明猫的帮助。
它想，你一个人钓鱼，一个人发呆，连鱼篓空空都没人笑你，以后不会了。
以后有猫啦。
en:
One day, while strolling through Wellspring Town, Leek spotted a wanderer fishing by the water.
The wanderer had a battered sword slung over their back and a miserably empty fish basket. Finally giving up for the day, the traveler reeled in the line, turned around, and spotted it. Smiling, the traveler reached out to give it a scratch.
Now, Leek was a cat of standing. A civilized feline. It was supposed to be far above such base animal instincts. And yet, before it even realized what it was doing, Leek had flopped right onto its back, all four paws in the air, baring its soft tummy and meowing away. It waited for the human to melt into the usual baby talk: "Who's a good kitty? Are you a sweet little kitty?" just like everyone else did.
But the traveler didn't coo. Instead, they just chuckled and said, "I've got a cat, too, you know. It's already my good kitty."
Liar! Leek huffed inwardly. Where is this invisible cat of yours, then?
Leek wanted to storm off, but for some reason, it didn't. Instead, it sat down next to the wanderer, neatly draping its tail over the edge of their sleeve. One human and one cat sat there, side by side, from dusk until the stars came out.
When the wanderer finally stood up to leave, Leek trotted along. "Are you coming with me?" the wanderer asked. Leek didn't dignify that with an answer, merely keeping up its elegant, measured pace.
Humans are such a handful, Leek sighed to itself. It had always assumed it was only stray kittens who needed the guidance of a civilized cat. It'd never realized humans needed looking after just as badly.
You sit out here fishing all by yourself, it thought, watching the human walk. You stare off into space all by yourself, and you don't even have anyone around to poke fun at your empty fish basket. Well, not anymore.
From now on, you have a cat.
...That sounds like something Ruby would say.

en:
Dragon's Breath is my family's secret art, passed down from a martial master of the former dynasty. My father wished to teach me this mystic skill, but in my youth, I dismissed such street performances as lowly tricks and refused to learn. I dreamed only of mastering sword and script, achieving great feats. For years, I wandered with my family, performing for a living.

One day, when war broke out, I found myself defenseless. Hiding in the shadows, I wept as my sister was lost. Just as blades were about to fall, my father arrived and used Dragon's Breath to drive back our foes and save us all. Only then did I realize that there are no lowly skills or inferior arts, for true strength lies in self-preservation and protecting others.

zh:
你入河西后，我便一直守着。看你忽而泣如幼子，又忽作狮子之吼。那声色慑人，倒真给我惹了不少麻烦。你呀你，还真是梦陷重渊，直把他乡作故乡呀。
长夜将明，该看的故事看了，该见的人见了，该走的地方也都走尽了。好梦收场，偏你应承我的事却抛诸脑后，诸多线索都视若无睹，真叫人生气。

罢了，不管如何，此行的尽头——秦川，你终究是到了。离那个秘密，也越来越近。就差这最后一点尾巴，你且少管些旁人闲事，多在正经物件上留心，或画具，或遗稿，总逃不过那几样，想来就算那老头藏得再严实，也总有破绽。

——不过，你要是真遇见那老头，最好远远走开。钟瓯相鸣，如水互注。若魂梦相交，必定——哼。
鸡鸣不已，我先去料理了那东西。你自行珍重。

我若拿不到我要的东西，你……也不必回来了。
en:
Since you crossed into Hexi, I have been watching over you. I have seen you weep like a child one moment and roar like a lion the next. That outburst of yours caused me no small amount of trouble. You really are something, so deep in your dream that you have taken a foreign land for home.
But the long night is nearly done. You have seen what there was to see, met who there was to meet, and walked every road that needed walking. A fine dream, and yet you cast aside the promise you made me, blind to every clue that lay before you. I will admit, that was aggravating.

No matter. Whatever else may be said, you have reached Qinchuan, the end of this road. The secret is close now, with only one loose thread remaining. Spend less time meddling in other people's affairs and more time watching for what matters: painting tools, manuscripts, the usual sorts of things. However carefully the old man has hidden it, there will be a crack somewhere.

One thing more: if you do happen to come face-to-face with that old man, walk away. The bell and the bowl ring in answer to each other; two waters poured together will mingle. If your souls and dreams should meet, the result will certainly be... hmph.
The cock will not stop crowing, and I have something to attend to. Take care of yourself.

If I do not get what I came for, there will be no reason for you to return.

zh:
石家村有一种人，叫做望汛人，博浪沙有一面鼓，叫做昭雪天听鼓。
鼓面有一道伤，那道伤从九六零年来。
那一年黄河洪水滔天，石家村的人敲破了鼓，却没叫回那本该救灾回援的望汛人。
那天，先是鼓声震天，愈来愈响。
后来，妻离子散的痛哭，孩童慌乱的叫喊嵌在这鼓声之中，鼓声渐渐盖不过哭声。
再后来，哭声停了，鼓声停了，哭的人死了，鼓也碎了。

鼓没有等来的那个人，叫做石守信。

昭雪天听鼓破碎的瞬间，他的新主黄袍加身，被他迎入开封，回师的军队仪仗声太响，也许，他实在听不见那哀求的鼓声。
他不再是望汛人，他是侍卫马步军副都指挥使，再后来他是同平章事，再升任侍卫马步军都指挥使。
石家村的人记不得这一长串难懂的官职，在石家村他的身份再也没有变过。
村中人看向他路过的父母：“呸，咱小村子可盛不下将军，当年的小石头？死了！”
那鼓面被打断的伤痕是他被打断的脊梁，他是众所周知的反骨仔，是踩在村中亲朋，旧日友人尸骨之上的背信弃义之人，是朱鱼之死的凶手之一，那些没有被理会的血泪在干涸之中变成了恨意的鸿沟。

石守信也再没有回到过石家村。
谁也不知道，当他站在庙堂之上时，看向某处蜿蜒的河流在岸边激起白浪，见到案卷上某地洪灾的呈报时，是否会想起一面被敲破的鼓，在他的耳边，那滔滔洪水又是否已经停歇，又或者根本从未响起。
en:
"In Shi Family Village, there were those called Flood Watchers. At Roaring Sands, there stood a drum: the Drum of Heavenly Vindication. A gash ran across its surface, a wound from the year 960.

That year, the Yellow River raged. The villagers beat the drum until it split, yet the Flood Watcher who should have returned with aid never came. At first, the drumming shook the skies, growing ever louder. Then, the wails of broken families and the frantic screams of children wove into its rhythm, until the drum could no longer drown out the crying. Finally, the weeping stopped. The drumming stopped. The weepers were dead. The drum was shattered.

The man the drum failed to summon was Shi Shouxin.

At the very moment the Drum of Heavenly Vindication shattered, his new lord donned the yellow robe of emperorship, escorted into Kaifeng. The ceremonial procession of the returning army was so thunderous that perhaps he truly could not hear the pleading drumbeats from his home.

He was no longer a Flood Watcher. He was Deputy Commander of the Imperial Guard, then Minister of Equal Rank, and later, Commander of the Imperial Guard. The people of Shi Family Village could not recall this long string of titles. To them, his identity had never changed. Villagers would look at his parents as they passed and spit, ""Our humble village can't hold a general. As for Little Shouxin? He's long dead!""

The gash that split the drumhead was the symbol of his own shattered spine. He was the notorious turncoat, a man who climbed to power over the bones of his kin and friends, one of the murderers of Zhu Yu. The unheeded blood and tears dried into a chasm of hatred.

Shi Shouxin never returned to Shi Family Village.

No one knows if, standing in the imperial court, seeing a winding river churn white waves, or reading official reports of a flood somewhere, he ever remembered a shattered drum. Did the roar of the flood ever fade from his ears? Or had it, for him, never truly sounded at all?"

他只是想听清那人最后一句嘱托：“快……”
快……什么？
听不见了，他只能听见那人好久好久之前的话：
“混小子！”

“这是我儿子，江晏！”
……
“快……”，风又急急催来，他将过往吞咽而下，向前出剑——
那柄临近新岁刚得的剑，王清请名家给他锻打的，寒光凛凛的好剑。
en:
When he reached the northern battlefield, the mist of blood and death tangled his blade. He had seen death before, from disasters and wars, but he simply was not ready. He only wanted to hear that last instruction: "Quick..."

Quick... what?

He could no longer hear. Only the memories of long ago echoed in his mind:
"You brat!"
"Oh? A new stance? Come, let's see what you've got!"
"The Northern Vow marches north soon. Who will meet them at Plowing Hill? You look eager, boy!"
"This is my son, Jiang Yan!"

"Quick..." the wind urged once more. He swallowed the past and thrust his sword forward: the very blade he received before the New Year, forged by a master at Wang Qing's request, a cold and shimmering masterpiece.

zh:
和人埋在雪里玩的时候，那人总嘀咕着什么边界感。
边界感是什么？满世界都是凉州的雪，雪从来就没有边界呀。
雪墩墩不懂。那个和自己玩得很好的人，最近居然溜了；身边还冒出来另一只雪墩墩，一点都不热乎，真没劲。
能爱人就很难得啦，哪知道爱得太满，也会让人发愁呢。
人竟然为了逃避雪墩墩的抱抱，不惜把自己裹在雪里，忍受天寒地冻，装作雪墩墩的同类。
墩好，人坏。算了算了。
至少，人终于能和雪墩墩并着肩，安静地看完这场雪。
en:
When it played in the snow with a human, the person kept muttering about “boundaries."

Boundaries? What are those? Liangzhou is nothing but snow. Since when did snow have edges?

The Snow Lion didn't understand.

The one who used to have the most fun with it had slipped away lately. And now there was another Snow Lion at its side, cold as ice and no fun at all.

Being able to warm up to people was rare enough. Who knew you could love too much and make them worry?

Just to dodge the Snow Lion's hugs, humans would wrap themselves in snow, shiver through the cold, and pretend to be one of its kind.

Snow Lions good. Humans bad. Fine, fine.

At least in the end, the human could stand shoulder to shoulder with the Snow Lion and quietly watch the snow fall.

en: "After King Wu passed and King Wen ascended the throne, Bian He clutched his uncut jade and wept at the foot of Mount Chu for three days and nights, until his tears ran dry and blood flowed instead. “我又写了新故事，看不看？看就汪一声，不看汪两声。”
“汪！”
“故事说的是，有一个小宫女……”
“汪！”
“认真听！汪汪侠！宫女名为璎璎，一直有一个大侠梦……起因没想好，经过也没想好，总之最后她成为了大侠，就跟越女、聂隐娘一样！怎么样？喜欢这个故事吗？喜欢的话，就汪一声，要是不喜欢……”
“汪！汪！汪！汪！汪！汪！汪……”
“汪汪侠！不许乱汪了。快说！喜不喜欢嘛？不喜欢我就改。”

汪汪侠听不懂什么故事，它只是觉得，眼前的人一次又一次找自己说这些话，她应该很喜欢这个故事吧。

“——汪！”
en:
"I wrote a new story. Want to hear it? One woof for yes, two woofs for no."
"Woof!"

"It's about a young palace maid..."
"Woof!"

"Listen up, Bark Knight. Her name is Yingying, and she's always dreamed of becoming a great hero..."
"I haven't figured out the beginning. Or the middle. Anyway, in the end she becomes a hero, just like the sword-wielding heroines in storybooks! So? Do you like it? If you do, give me one woof. If you don't..."

"Woof! Woof! Woof! Woof! Woof! Woof! Woof..."

"Bark Knight. No more nonsense woofing. Tell me, do you like it or not? If you don't, I'll change it."

Bark Knight doesn't understand stories.
It only knows the person in front of it keeps coming back to say these things, again and again. They must really love that story.

沿墨城向东数十里，可见高山云海，时有连珠落盘之声，以为仙人垂泪。定睛上视，见一云槎穿空入云，上御疾风星驰，下踏奔浪逐波。
同行者谓，此乃墨门云槎揽胜。
只憾乘舟须备令牌，唯有内门名列前茅者有此殊恩。

en:
Old legends tell of a fairy mountain in the East Sea, reachable only by a mystical floating raft. Every mid-autumn, the gates to the immortal realm open, drawing adventurous souls eager to find the elusive peak.
A few dozen miles east of Mohist City, towering peaks rise through sea clouds. Sometimes, faint clinking sounds, said to be the immortals' tears, can be heard. Look closely, and you might see a cloud-raft slicing through the sky, rushing on fierce winds and chasing waves below. Locals say it's the Sky Shuttle of the Mohist. But only top inner disciples, holding special tokens, are allowed aboard.
When I asked how long the wait might be, the reply was a sigh: "By then, the seas will have turned to dust. It is a heartbreak beyond words."

zh:
盖闻前世同船渡，今朝共枕眠。
上官何人竟遇柳氏思安。
一日夫妻自有齐眉之意，百日恩情则是执手之心。
上官与安娘本欲看尽长安风流，揽月长歌。
成佳偶而他人艳羡，造伉俪而天地同欢。
奈何流年生间隙，身不由己，世事多艰险，忿谷难平。
安娘柔若蒲柳，良善温婉，却上不可侍奉姑婆，下不堪安治家宅。
今放安娘，欢喜自生。伏愿娘子，再觅良家。
饮花对月，儿孙满膝。六族欢喜，上官无憾。
为留后凭，长安万年县，
上官泽谨立
en:
It is said that a shared boat in a past life grants a shared pillow in this one. What great fortune, then, was mine to have met you, Lady Liu Si'an.

To be husband and wife for a day is to share mutual respect; for a hundred days, it is the bond of holding hands into old age. With you, I had wished to witness all of Chang'an's splendor, to sing long songs beneath the moon. To be a perfect couple, envied by others; to be true partners, celebrated by Heaven and Earth.

Alas, the passing years created a rift between us. Our lives were not our own to command, and the world is fraught with hardship and sorrow. You, Si'an, gentle as a willow, virtuous and kind, were yet unable to serve the elders above, nor manage the household below.

Today, I restore to you your freedom, hoping it brings you joy. I humbly pray that you, my lady, will find another good family. May you drink among blossoms and gaze upon the moon, with children and grandchildren gathered at your knees. May your family rejoice, and I, Shangguan, shall have no regrets.

This letter is set down as proof.

In Wannian County of Chang'an.

Respectfully,
Shangguan Ze

zh:
涌泉镇者，在青州之南，岱岳之东。其地多泉，甲于海岱。昔时有泺水出于岩，泉源涌沸，高或至数尺，声若雷鸣，乡人呼为“爆流泉”。千百年间，泉脉不绝，除四眼大泉之外，又有小泉六十有八，合为七十二泉，散落镇中，或如珍珠，或如卧牛，或如奔马，或如龙吟，姿态各异，不可尽述。



文津馆长乐老，尝携十相游历至此，观泉流连，叹为奇观。见四泉最为雄壮，乃一一命名：其一曰卧牛泉，泉畔巨石如牛卧水，水浸其腹，泠然有声；其二曰马跑泉，相传战马刨地得水，蹄痕犹存；其三曰珍珠泉，泉底涌珠，累累不绝，日光下彻，灿若繁星；其四曰五龙泉，泉分五脉，汇于一池，水势浩荡。长乐老又合四泉与诸小泉，总名之曰“四海生平泉”，寓天下升平、文运昌隆之意。自是泉名远播，四方皆知。



涌泉镇因泉而兴。商队不远万里，驱车而至，汲泉装瓮，运销他乡。其水甘冽，久贮不腐，或烹茶，或酿酒，或入药，皆称上品。又有观光雅士，结伴而来，临泉吟诗，对月把盏，题壁留墨，岁久成集。镇中酒肆茶楼，多挂“天下第一泉”之匾，亦彰其名之盛。



镇之得名，则另有故实。昔魏晋八王之乱，一文官避兵至此，夜闻泉声，掘地得活水，乃叹曰：“天下血涌如泉，此地文如泉涌。”遂率流亡结庐垦荒，开蒙识字，名其地曰涌泉。后唐末乱世，文津馆率乡民筑蒙学馆于镇中，立学规“稚子必开蒙，家贫毋辍书”，男女同席，书声与泉声相和，至今不辍。



今游涌泉者，掬水而饮，但觉清冽入喉，似有千年文气。泉眼无声，日夜涌流；书声琅琅，世代不绝。一泉一书，斯镇之魂也。



嗟乎！天下名泉多矣，或以清冽称，或以奇景著。而涌泉之水，不唯润物，更以文脉相传。昔人云“文如泉涌”，此地实兼而有之。后人至此，当知泉之妙处，不在石上，而在人心。
en:
Wellspring Town is located to the south of Qingzhou and the east of Mount Tai. The land is abundant with springs, crowning all the lands between Mount Tai and the sea. In ancient times, the River Luo flowed from these rocks. The source boiled and surged, sometimes reaching several feet in height, roaring like thunder. The locals called it the Bursting Torrent Spring. For over a millennium, the water veins have never dried. Aside from the four great springs, there are sixty-eight lesser ones, making seventy-two springs in total scattered throughout the town. Some resemble pearls, others resting oxen, galloping steeds, or chanting dragons. Their forms are so diverse they cannot be fully described.
Elder Feng Dao of the Inkbound Order once traveled here with the Ten Sages. Captivated by the flowing waters, he praised them as a supreme marvel. Noting that the four main springs were the most majestic, he named them one by one. The first was Resting Ox Spring: a massive boulder by the water resembled an ox lying in the shallows, the current lapping at its belly with a crystalline chime. The second was Pawing Steed Spring: legend tells that a warhorse struck the earth to find water, and hoofprints still remain. The third was Pearl Spring: bubbles rise from the bottom in an endless string, sparkling like a sky of stars beneath the sunlight. The fourth was Five Dragons Spring: five water veins converge into a single pool, surging with immense power. Elder Changle then grouped these four with the lesser springs, crowning them collectively as the Springs of Universal Peace, symbolizing a harmonious world and a flourishing era of literature. From then on, the names of the springs spread far and wide, known to the four corners of the earth.
Wellspring Town prospered because of its waters. Merchant caravans travel thousands of miles, driving their carts to draw the spring water into urns, selling it in distant lands. The water is sweet and crisp, never spoiling even after long storage. Whether used for brewing tea, fermenting wine, or preparing medicine, it is hailed as top-tier. Refined scholars also arrive in groups, chanting poetry by the waters, raising cups to the moon, and leaving their calligraphy on the cliffsides, which over the years has formed grand anthologies. Many taverns and teahouses in town hang plaques reading "The Finest Spring Under Heaven," further manifesting its towering fame.
The town's naming, however, holds another tale. During the Rebellion of the Eight Princes in the Wei and Jin dynasties, a civil official fled the chaos of war and arrived here. Hearing the sound of water at night, he dug into the earth and discovered a living spring. He sighed, saying, "While the realm bleeds a fountain of blood, this land shall well up a fountain of letters." He then led the refugees to build cottages and clear the wasteland, initiating basic schooling and literacy, and named the place Wellspring.
Later, during the turmoil at the end of the Tang Dynasty, the Inkbound Order led the locals to establish a Primary Academy within the town. They set a rule: "The young must be enlightened. Poverty shall halt no one's studies." Boys and girls shared the same seats, and the sound of reading resonated with the bubbling springs, a tradition unbroken to this day.
Today, those who visit Wellspring Town and scoop the water to drink will feel a crisp coolness slide down their throats, seemingly imbued with a thousand years of literary spirit. The springs flow silently, day and night; the bright sound of reading rings out, generation after generation. A spring, a book: these are the very soul of this town.
Alas! There are many famous springs in the world. Some are praised for their clarity, others famed for their peculiar sights. Yet the waters of Wellspring not only nourish the earth but carry forth the lineage of culture. The ancients said, "Culture wells up like a spring," and this place truly embodies both. Future generations arriving here should know that the true marvel of these springs lies not upon the rocks, but within the hearts of men.

zh:
演武为3v3公平竞技玩法，在该玩法中少侠的战斗属性将进行调平，角色各属性值一致，装备套装和止戈定音效果支持自选，奇术为6重40段，心法为6重，止戈天赋解锁当前赛季所有通用型天赋。食物和符帖效果在玩法中不生效。

匹配规则：同一队伍内最多只能有2名游侠使用相同的武学，最多1名游侠携带治疗武学。

演武玩法中，最多可使用20支箭矢，治疗效果降低70%。进入战斗一段时间后，玩家伤害将获得提升且治疗效果将进一步下降。在#Y无治疗流派#E的对局中全队共获得一次复活机会。队友倒下15秒内，在其阵亡位置10米范围内可将其复活。被复活的队友将获得20%外功攻击提升，持续20秒。在#Y有治疗流派#E的对局中，武学明川药典感知技千金朝玉仅可使用1次，心法君臣药六重效果不受此限制。#Y小队面板上的复活次数显示未计入“君臣药”六重效果带来的额外次数#E。

场景机制：雪天战场处于极寒环境，#Y火属性伤害降低50%#E，影响神龙吐火、流星坠火、火箭。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。玩法中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。解控技能清风霁月可在受击或控制状态下使用，活用可以有效扭转劣势。

移动端与PC端为独立的匹配池。组队参与玩法时，匹配逻辑遵循以下规则：系统将检测队伍内所有成员的设备类型。一旦检测到存在PC端设备，该队伍会被纳入PC端匹配队列。若玩家在移动端匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方全部玩家的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
3v3 Arena is a fair competitive mode where combat attributes are balanced. All character attributes are normalized. Gear sets and Arena Attunement effects are customizable. Mystic Skills are at Tier 6 Rank 40, and Inner Ways are at Tier 6. All general Arena Talents for the current season are unlocked. Food and Talisman effects are inactive.

Matching Rules: A team can have a maximum of 2 players using the same martial art and 1 player using healing martial arts.

In 3v3 Arena, a maximum of 20 arrows can be used, and healing effects are reduced by 70%. After a certain duration in combat, damage increases and healing further decreases. Teams #Ywithout a healer#E receive one revival attempt. Fallen teammates can be revived within 10m of their death location within 15s. Revived players gain a 20% Physical Attack bonus for 20s. In matches with #Yhealers#E, Panacea Fan's perception skill: Resurrection can only be used once. Tier 6 effect of Royal Remedy is not affected by this limit. #YResurrection counts on the team panel do not include extra counts from the Tier 6 Royal Remedy effect#E.

Scene Mechanism: Snowy battlefields are extremely cold. #YFire damage is reduced by 50%#E for Dragon's Breath, Flaming Meteor, and Flaming Arrow.

Most skills can be countered with Deflect. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills cannot be deflected and deal enhanced damage to targets using Defense or Deflect, but can be interrupted by any skill. Using Deflect costs Endurance, while landing an Execution restores it. Player skills (including Mystic and Charged) can interrupt Light/Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. Use Break Control Skills like Serene Breeze to escape control effects.

Mobile and PC players queue separately. In team queue, if any member is using a PC, the entire team enters the PC matchmaking pool. Players showing abnormal cross-platform behavior (e.g., account takeover) on mobile will be moved to the PC queue.

Win by eliminating all opponents. If time expires, victory is decided by:
1. Surviving players
2. Total damage
3. Total healing.

zh:
一
李昭雪站在长安城外的渭水桥上。
对面是叛军的精锐，黑压压一片，旗帜在暮色中翻卷如鸦群。风从东边来，带着烧焦的味道——昨夜城外粮草被焚，几里外还能闻到烟火气。
皇宫里已经没有人了。高官贵族闻风而逃，车马从清晨一直走到日暮。只有百姓还留在城里。不是不想走，是不知道往哪走。这座城是他们的家乡，是他们引以为傲的繁华，是他们祖祖辈辈安安稳稳的日子。城在，他们在。城若破了——
李昭雪没有想下去。
他站在最前面。没有人请他来。他已经七十多岁了。
作为一个武功高手，这个岁数也不容忽视——但“不容忽视”和“寄予厚望”是两回事。没有人指望一个七十多岁的老人来守城，但没有人不指望李昭雪来。他本可以像其他人一样，骑马往南走，走到江南，走到剑南，走到叛军追不上的地方。
但他没有走。不是因为勇武，是因为他也发现自己无处可去。他的一辈子，都在身后这座城里。城若破了，他往哪走都是逃。

二
他想起自己二十岁的时候。
那时候他意气风发，一柄长剑走天下。在大军溃败时，他护着骆宾王一路撤走，朝廷发了海捕文书，请了高手截杀他，他不在意。他只是不想让那个写“鹅鹅鹅”的老人死在乱军之中。那时候的他不怕朝廷，不怕追杀，不怕任何东西。他觉得自己能赢一切。
后来他回了长安，被绑着进了皇宫，又站着走出来。
走回道真的这一路，一共有七十二个人拦他，一个接一个挑战他。他没有退。
那一日，道真门前的大道上躺了七十二个人，七十二个江湖有名有姓的人。他站在道路的尽头，看见李无量开了道真的大门迎接他。
长剑归鞘，月光照着他的脸，年轻，骄傲，不知疲倦。
再后来……
再后来李无量去世了，道真在动荡中交到了他手上。
再再后来，江湖围剿魔头——那是雩真第一次被叫做魔头。各派高手还有掌门住持门主什么的去了十多位，却被她耍得团团转，最后折损过半。他不知该作何感想，只是如约站了出来。他要稳住局面。
他降服了雩真，受伤的雩真。所有人说，杀了她，以绝后患。从最早的邙山约战之事，到后来的追捕，有太多的新仇旧怨滋生。千夫所指，众口铄金。
他没有杀。他把她关进了岱山深处的山洞。
江湖人不理解，但反对者都被他压下。魔头关起来了，大家安心了。他们转头忍下不满，说他仁义，说他顾全大局。
只有他自己知道，那不是仁义。

三
几十年来，所有人都知道，江湖有一座山，叫做李昭雪。
他在，江湖就心安。就如同开元天宝的盛世光景一样——只要他还在，好像什么都不会倒。
可现在，盛世不再了。叛军破关，要塞沦陷，皇帝出逃。那座山还在，但山老了。
他老了。
他每天早上醒来，膝盖僵硬，要坐在床边缓一缓。夜里睡不踏实，一点声响就醒，醒了就再也睡不着。他的皮肤松了，手背上的青筋像蚯蚓一样鼓着。他还在练剑，但只是熟练，不再精进。他还在打坐，但内息运转时，偶尔会有阻滞——像一条河，流着流着，遇到了一块搬不走的石头。
他停在了功法第十一层。三十年前是第十一层，三十年后还是第十一层。这就是他的极限。他早就知道了。
但他没有告诉任何人。在别人眼里，他还是那座山。
四
又一波敌人冲上来了。
叛军在折损了五员大将之后，换了策略。不再派高手来送死，换上了行伍小兵。一个一个上，一批一批上。用车轮战，用命来填。他们想把李昭雪活活累死。
李昭雪挥剑，斩杀，再挥剑，再斩杀。动作已经不如从前快了，但每一剑还是精准的，还是致命的。
他的思绪却飘远了。
他想起了李无量。
据说，李无量从邙山之战出来的时候，就已经有了天人五衰的症状。可他还是活了一百二十岁。他的徒子徒孙都死在邙山了，后半生他一直在找一个继承人。找了很久，找到了一个“孙女”。
李昭雪以前听到这桩旧事时，还不懂什么叫天人五衰。现在他懂了。
是你的眼睛不再锐利，看清远处的东西要眯起眼。是你的丹田不再雄浑，运气时像挑着一副担子。是你运功时偶尔会轻微地顿一下。那一瞬间，你心里会慌。是你开始模糊一些应该记得的名字——明明就在嘴边，却怎么也叫不出来。
没有人看出这些。他们眼中的李昭雪依然是那座山。但李昭雪自己知道。
几十年前他就知道了。
那时候雩真刚刚崭露头角。他看着她练武，一招一式，像是天生就会。他心里忽然有一个声音说：她和你一样强。
不是“将来和你一样强”。是现在，就一样强。
他不想承认，但他骗不了自己。
时间把一个同样的天才放在他面前，过早地、猝不及防地，告诉他，嘲笑他——你抵抗不了。
二十年的岁数差距，在凡人中，是一代人的传承。幸运之极。可在学武之人当中，却远远不够。若是传承，太短；若是同辈，太长。不巧之极。
他还未从台前退下，同样优秀的后辈，就已站上台来。就像月挂中天，却有第二轮新月将满。
他不甘心。
他如何甘心？
这武道巅峰怎能放过，这世间之极他还要推得更远。他凭什么退，他为何要退？为何是他退？ 
时间没有说话，只是冷笑看他。
因为他生得早了。因为雩真也生得早了。
一个早生了二十年，一个也早生了二十年——不是她来得太晚，是他来得太早。
这是世上最差劲的相逢。

五
一只冷箭擦过他的衣角，钉在身后，嗡地颤了一下。
仿佛也在冷笑他的走神，冷笑他此刻的衰老。
他比三十多年前更老了。没有了雩真——不，正因为没有了雩真——他还是要面临这一刻。他还是站在这里，一个人，面对一支军队。
他抬了抬眼，看到的不是敌人，还是时间。
源源不断的大军，换将换人地磨他。就像时间日复一日地拿走他康健的身体，他敏锐的头脑，他顺畅的呼吸。拿走他的头发，他的牙齿，他的睡眠，他的胃口，他的记性。拿走他的骄傲，他的不服，他的“我还可以”。
凭什么？
李昭雪怒上心头，昭雪剑也发出鸣叫。对着无可战胜的时间，对着这荒唐的一切。吼叫！吼叫！吼叫!
凭什么！
他握紧了昭雪剑。眼前是黑压压的敌军，是无尽的战场，是永远杀不完的兵。和时间的战争没有尽头，没有人会胜利。
但他还是站起来了。在不知道多少人的车轮战后，在所有追随者都死去，在所有敌人都以为他早该死去的此刻——他又站了起来。
他的膝盖不再发冷，他的牙齿不再酸软，他的眼睛不再浑浊。
他的剑，和以前一样。
不，比以前更利。
这一剑，还在昭告天下，此为李昭雪。

六
几天后，新一波叛军赶到了渭水桥。
他们看到桥上的尸体——自己人的尸体，铺了一地。桥中央站着一个人，白发披散，浑身是血，长剑拄地，纹丝不动。
领兵的将领怒斥停在这里的同僚：“一群废物！一个人挡了你们这么久？！”
他亲自走上前去，要会一会这昭雪剑。
待走到那人面前，新将领却两股颤颤。那人微张着眼，面容平静，像只是在小憩。但在旁人看来，他仿佛一座庞然大物，就像他身后的长安城。
多少人畏惧它，多少人仰望它，多少人想践踏它。
良久，将领终于回过神来，敢伸手一摸。
触手僵硬，冰凉如铁。
李昭雪已经死去多时了。
他们不过是被这一具尸体，吓破了胆，徒困了十日而已。
没有人敢动那具尸体。也没有人敢收。他就那样站在桥上，拄着剑，面向北方——面向叛军来的方向。
背向他守了一辈子的城。
风吹过渭水，吹动他的白发，吹不动他的剑。
李昭雪。这三个字，他刻在了时间之上。
en:
I
Li Zhaoxue stood upon the Wei River Bridge, just beyond the gates of Chang'an.
Across the water lay the vanguard of the rebel horde, a suffocating, iron-black tide. In the dying light, their banners thrashed against the dusk like a murder of crows. The wind blew from the east, heavy with the bitter scent of ash. The granaries outside the gates had been torched the night before, and even miles away, the air was still thick with the smoke of ruin.
The imperial palace was already empty. At the first whisper of danger, the high ministers and noble houses had scattered. From dawn until dusk, an exodus of fine carriages and galloping horses had choked the roads leading out of the capital. Only the commoners remained. It wasn't that they lacked the will to flee. They simply had nowhere else to go. This city was their homeland. It was the glittering prosperity they took such fierce pride in. It was the quiet, anchored lives their ancestors had built, generation upon generation. While the walls stood, they stood. If the city fell...
Li Zhaoxue did not let himself finish the thought.
He stood at the very front of the bridge. No one had asked him to come. He was an old man, well past his seventieth year.
For a martial grandmaster, such an age still commanded a heavy measure of dread, but commanding dread and offering salvation are two very different things. No one in their right mind expects a septuagenarian to defend a besieged capital single-handedly. And yet, there wasn't a single soul in Chang'an who hadn't prayed for Li Zhaoxue to appear.
He could have done exactly what the lords did. He could have saddled a fast horse and ridden south to Jiangnan or Jiannan, vanishing into sanctuaries the rebel blades could never reach.
But he did not leave. It was not out of some fierce, untamed heroism, but out of a quiet, unshakable truth: he, too, had nowhere else to go. His entire life, every memory and ounce of meaning, was etched into the ancient stones of the city behind him. If Chang'an fell, no matter how far he rode, the rest of his life would be nothing but flight.

II
He remembered what it was to be twenty.
Drunk on his own untamed brilliance, he had wandered the mortal realm with nothing but a longsword. When the great armies shattered, he had personally escorted Luo Binwang through the carnage to safety. The imperial court had issued bounty hunting warrants for his head and unleashed their deadliest hounds to intercept him, but he hadn't cared. He simply refused to let the gentle old poet, the man who had written the Ode to the Goose, be trampled into the mud of war. Back then, he feared nothing. Not the throne, not the blades in the dark, not death itself. He believed the world was his to conquer.
Later, he returned to Chang'an. He was taken to the imperial palace in chains, yet he walked out on his own two feet.
On the long, lonely road back to the Daozhen Sect, seventy-two men blocked his path. One by one, they drew their steel. He never took a single step back.
That day, seventy-two bodies littered the grand avenue leading to Daozhen's gates, seventy-two of the most formidable names in the jianghu. He stood at the end of that bloodied road, watching as Li Wuliang pushed open the heavy wooden gates to welcome him home.
As he slid his sword back into its scabbard, the moonlight fell across his face: impossibly young, fiercely proud, and utterly tireless.
And then...
And then Li Wuliang passed away, and the crushing weight of the Daozhen Sect was thrust upon his shoulders just as the realm descended into chaos.
And then came the great crusade. That was the very first time Yuzhen had ever been branded a "demon." Over a dozen of the realm's most revered masters, including sect masters, grand abbots, and clan masters, rode out to hunt her down, only to be led on a lethal, humiliating dance. By the end, half of them were dead. He hadn't known what to feel. He simply stepped forward, just as the world demanded of him. He had to hold the collapsing realm together.
He subdued Yuzhen. An already wounded Yuzhen. The entire jianghu screamed for her execution, desperate to sever the root of future disaster. From the first fateful duel at Mount Mang to the endless, bloody pursuits that followed, too many bitter grudges had been sown. Condemned by thousands, the sheer weight of public hatred demanded her head.
But he did not kill her. Instead, he sealed her away in a lightless cavern deep within Mount Tai.
The sects were furious, but he ruthlessly crushed all dissent. With the demon locked in the dark, the realm could finally sleep. Swallowing their bloodlust, the world turned around and praised his boundless mercy, lauding him as a visionary who prioritized the greater good.
But only he knew the truth. It had never been mercy.

III
For decades, the jianghu held fast to a single, unshakable truth: there was a mountain standing over them, and its name was Li Zhaoxue.
As long as he stood, the realm felt secure. He was the living embodiment of the empire's golden age. As long as he remained, it felt as though the sky itself could not fall.
But the golden age was dead. The rebels had shattered the mountain passes, the fortresses had fallen, and the emperor had fled. The mountain was still standing, but the mountain had grown old.
He was old.
Every morning, he woke to knees so stiff he had to sit on the edge of his bed just to wait for the ache to dull. His nights were fractured and thin. The rustle of a leaf would wake him, and once awake, sleep would never return. His skin was withered, the veins on the backs of his hands bulging like knotted roots. He still practiced his forms, but it was merely the rote maintenance of muscle memory. There were no more breakthroughs. He still meditated, but his internal breath would occasionally catch and stagnate, like a dying river failing to push past a stone.
His cultivation had stalled at the eleventh tier. Thirty years ago, he was at the eleventh tier; thirty years later, he was there still. It was his absolute limit. He had known this for a long time.
But he never breathed a word of it to a living soul. To the rest of the world, he was still the invincible mountain.

IV
Another wave of enemies surged onto the bridge.
Having lost five of their greatest generals to his blade, the rebels had changed their tactics. They no longer sent masters to throw their lives away. They sent the infantry, rank after rank, wave after wave. They would pave their way across the river with an endless tide of bodies. They intended to bleed Li Zhaoxue of his stamina and grind him into the dust.
Li Zhaoxue swung his sword. A man fell. He swung again. Another fell.
His blade was not as blindingly fast as it once was, but every strike was precise. Every strike was fatal.
Yet, amidst the mindless rhythm of slaughter, his thoughts drifted far away.
He thought of Li Wuliang.
It was said that when Li Wuliang emerged from the bloodbath at Mount Mang, he was already exhibiting the Five Decays of the Celestial. Yet, through sheer, stubborn will, he clung to life until he was a hundred and twenty. His disciples and grand-disciples had all perished in the carnage, leaving him to spend the twilight of his life wandering in search of an heir. He searched for a very long time, until finally, he found a "granddaughter."
When Li Zhaoxue first heard this tale in his youth, he had not understood what the Five Decays truly meant. He understood it now.
It is the quiet dulling of your eyes, forcing you to squint to make out the horizon. It is the realization that your dantian is no longer a boundless well. Gathering your Qi feels like hoisting a crushing yoke of iron. It is that terrifying fraction of a second when your power stutters, a fleeting heartbeat where cold, breathless panic grips you. It is the fading of names you should know by heart, names that hover uselessly on the tip of your tongue, refusing to be spoken.
No one else saw the rot. To the rest of the world, Li Zhaoxue remained the invincible, unshakable mountain. But Li Zhaoxue knew.
He had known for decades.
Back then, Yuzhen was just beginning to forge her legend. He had watched her move through her forms, every stance, every strike flowing with a terrifying, innate perfection. And in that moment, a quiet voice whispered in his mind: She is your equal.
Not "one day, she will equal you." She was his equal. Right then. Right there.
He hadn't wanted to admit it, but he could not lie to himself. Time had thrust an absolute peer before him far too soon, catching him entirely off guard. It was Time's way of mocking him, of proving that this was a tide he could not hold back.
A gap of twenty years. In the mortal world, this is the span of a generation, the perfect rhythm for inheritance. A profound blessing. But for those who walk the martial path, it is a devastating misalignment. Too brief for a master to gently pass the torch; too wide for the two of them to be true peers. It was the cruelest trick of timing.
He had not yet stepped down from the pinnacle, yet an equally brilliant successor had already stepped up to claim the summit. It was like a blinding full moon hanging at its zenith, only to find a second moon rising beside it, growing brighter by the day.
He refused to accept it. How could he?
How could he surrender the martial peak? He still hungered to push the absolute limits of the mortal realm even further. By what right should he retreat? Why did he have to be the one to step aside into the shadows?
Time offered no answers. It only watched him with a cold, mocking sneer.
One was born twenty years too early, and tragically, so was the other. It wasn't that she had arrived too late. It was that he had arrived too soon.
It was the most tragic collision of fates the world had ever known.

V
A stray arrow clipped the hem of his robes, sinking into the earth behind him with a shivering hum.
It felt as though the arrow itself were mocking him, mocking his fractured focus, mocking the brittle frailty of his age. He was so much older now than he had been thirty years ago. Without Yuzhen, no, because he had chosen to erase Yuzhen, he was doomed to face this hour anyway. To stand here, utterly alone, against an empire in ruin.
He lifted his eyes. It was not an army he saw before him. It was Time itself.
The endless horde of soldiers ground him down, rank after rank, wave after wave. It was exactly how Time had ground him to dust, day by grueling day, ruthlessly stripping away his vitality, his sharp mind, the steady rhythm of his breath. Plundering his hair, his teeth, his sleep, his appetite, his memory. Hollowing out his pride, his defiance, his desperate, stubborn illusion that "I can still fight."
By what right?
A blazing, uncontrollable fury erupted in Li Zhaoxue's chest. In his hand, his sword began to sing, vibrating with a violent, blood-chilling resonance. Against the invincible, crushing march of Time. Against the sheer, wretched absurdity of fate.
It roared! It roared! It roared!
By what right?!
His fingers tightened like a vise around the hilt. Before him lay a suffocating tide of black iron, a battlefield without end, a swarm of men that could never truly be slaughtered to the last. The war against Time has no end, and no mortal can ever win it.
But he stood tall anyway.
After weathering an unimaginable slaughter, after every soul who had ever followed him had perished, at the exact moment his enemies believed his broken body should have finally collapsed into the mud, he stood.
His knees no longer ached with the cold. His jaw no longer trembled. His eyes were no longer clouded with the fog of age.
His sword was exactly as it had been in his youth.
No. It was sharper than ever before.
This single, blinding strike would still proclaim to the heavens: Here stands Li Zhaoxue.

VI
Days later, a fresh wave of rebel reinforcements arrived at the Wei River Bridge.
They found the stone span choked with the dead, their own dead. At the heart of the carnage stood a single man. His white hair blew wildly in the wind, his robes heavy and soaked in dark blood. He rested his weight upon a longsword planted in the earth, completely motionless.
The arriving commander sneered at the vanguard forces huddled uselessly at the edge of the bridge. "A pack of cowards! One man held you back this long?"
He marched forward himself, eager to cross blades with the legendary Zhaoxue.
But as he drew near, a sudden, icy dread gripped his chest. His knees began to tremble. The old master's eyes were half-open, his face as tranquil as if he had merely paused to rest. Yet, to anyone standing in his shadow, he exuded a suffocating, monumental weight. He was a monolith, immovable, exactly like the towering walls of Chang'an at his back. A titan that so many feared, so many revered, and so many hungered to trample into the dust.
After a long, breathless eternity, the commander finally broke free from his trance. He reached out a trembling hand and touched the old man.
His flesh was rigid, cold as iron.
Li Zhaoxue had been dead for days.
An entire rebel army had been paralyzed by their own terror, halted in their tracks for ten days by a corpse.
No one dared to move the body. No one dared to claim it. He simply remained standing on the blood-soaked bridge, anchored by his sword, facing north, staring down the path of the invading horde.
Forever, he stood with his back to the city he had spent a lifetime defending.
The wind howled across the Wei River, whipping wildly through his white hair. But it could not move his blade.
Li Zhaoxue. He had carved those three syllables into the very bedrock of Time.

zh: 花酒的酿造由来已久。屈原在《九歌》中即有“蕙肴蒸兮兰藉，奠桂酒兮椒浆”之句，枚乘亦在《七发》中写道“兰英之酒，酌以涤口”。百姓与雅士，皆好以花入酒，品其芬芳。而鬼市子的“黄泉酿”，便是取金灯花花蕊与黄泉水酿造而成的一道花酒。据传十余年前，有一醉客入鬼市，见那河岸边的金灯花风华绮丽，心念一动，便取花蕊，入黄泉水，酿作黄泉酒。而他饮下后，竟见生平最璀璨之事，最执拗之念，皆于眼前重现。此酒一出，商客皆蜂拥而来；而鬼市子之人闻之皆大惊失色。薛丑称黄泉水与金灯花皆带毒，意欲阻拦。然医师涂山允研究后发觉，两毒相抵，竟反成佳酿。此黄泉酿，遂于鬼市子留存至今。
en: The tradition of floral wines runs deep. In Nine Songs, Qu Yuan wrote, "We pour pepper sauce and laurel wine; serve spiced meat in orchid bowls." Mei Cheng, in Qifa, noted, "Orchid wine, used to rinse the mouth." From commoners to scholars, all delighted in infusing blossoms into their brews. In the Ghostlight Market, the famed Netherworld Wine is made from red spider lily stamens steeped in the waters of Huang Quan. Legend says that over a decade ago, a drunken wanderer, captivated by the lilies blooming along the riverbank, plucked a few stamens and brewed them with the underworld's water. Upon drinking it, he claimed to see his brightest memories and deepest longings come vividly to life. The brew quickly drew throngs of curious merchants. But locals were alarmed. Xue Chou warned that both the flowers and the water were poisonous. Yet after careful study, Physician Tushan discovered the toxins neutralized each other, creating something wholly new. Since then, Netherworld Wine has remained one of the Ghostlight Market's most coveted secrets.

叔父： 
距那夜佛堂叔父与我密谈，已十二载过去。

那时您说，禄伯，你既接此旗，我有三事托你。
我满口应承，心想世间事若我奋力而为，岂有做不到的？

三事其一，佑百姓温饱，其二，护边陲太平。
我与您相约，若得丰收，便以吉金铸六畜兴旺之礼送至长安。您说四畜即可，吉金还是多留些给百姓铸农具吧。 
至于第三事……等我完成了这两事再告诉我。

而今，边陲阡陌之间，百姓今年新种之苗已初现新绿，凉州亦再复归。承托的二事均已办妥，您未说的第三事……到底是什么？
en:
Uncle,
Twelve years have passed since our secret talk in the Buddhist shrine that night.
You said to me then, "Huaishen, since you have taken up this banner, there are three behests I must entrust to you." I agreed without hesitation, believing that if I fought with all my might, nothing in this world would be beyond my reach.

The first was to ensure the people are fed and clothed. The second, to safeguard the frontier's peace.
We agreed that upon a bountiful year, we would forge a bronze Harvest Tribute and send it to Chang'an. You said four beasts would suffice for the tribute, wishing to spare the remaining bronze for the people to forge farming tools.
As for the third behest... you told me to complete the first two before you would reveal it.

Now, fresh green shoots are sprouting across the borderlands, and Liangzhou has been fully restored. The first two behests you entrusted to me are done. What exactly is the third?

帝曰：“空手而归，敢欺朕耶？”
臣对曰：“臣袖中尚遗一核。可种上林。三千年后结实，未知陛下牙口尚佳否？”因出三核以献。
帝大笑，赦之。
en:
Tenth month, the second year of Tianhan.
Upon my return, I was granted an audience with His Majesty. He asked, "Did you obtain it?"
I prostrated myself and said, "I reached Mount Kunlun and paid my respects to the Queen Mother of the West, pleading for the elixir of immortality. Hearing Your Majesty's name, the Mother hosted a banquet for me. During the feast, she brought forth a peach and said to me, 'This peach bears fruit once every three thousand years. Eating it extends one's life by a century.' I was about to conceal it to present to Your Majesty, but then I thought a century was not enough, so I stole three more peaches. I was caught by the Giant Spirit. The Mother was furious and banished me back."
His Majesty said, "You returned empty-handed, yet dare to deceive me?"
I replied, "There are still peach pits in my sleeve. They may be planted in the Imperial Garden. In three thousand years they will bear fruit, though whether Your Majesty's teeth will still be strong enough by then, I cannot say." I then took out three pits and offered them.
His Majesty burst into laughter and pardoned me.

⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛

At Confluence Gazebo, they recount history; at the Disputation Platform, they debate the ages. With storms brewing of late, the debate between Expansion and Seclusion has become the center of daily discourse.

Knowing his distaste for disputes, you step forward to bail him out:

The crowd falls into a stunned silence. Seizing the moment while they reflect, you pull Feng through the throng in one swift motion. Once your breath is caught, you look him up and down. Something about Feng seems different, though you can't quite put your finger on it. Just then, a gust of wind sweeps by. Feng instinctively feels his head...
The good news: despite his devotion to research, Feng's hair remains thick and lush!
The bad news: his hat was left behind in Confluence Gazebo...

en:
When the birds are gone, the bow is laid aside. After the "Cup of Wine Policy" to disarm generals, military officials fell from power, and civil bureaucrats dominated. During this upheaval, Grand Councilor Zhao Pu was attacked in his mansion—only to be saved by the Star Stealer, a legendary thief who had vanished from the Jianghu for years. 
Rumors abound: Who sent the assassin? What is the relationship between the Star Stealer and Zhao Pu? Why did the thief appear in Zhao's mansion? 
Most intriguingly, the Star Stealer stole the renowned Canglang Sword Manual during the Wolf Mountain Battle years ago. 
Now that the Star Stealer has resurfaced, does it mean the mysterious manual will also reappear?

zh:
【仲尼燕居第二十八】

仲尼燕居，子张、子贡、言游侍，纵言至于礼。子曰：“居！女三人者，吾语女礼，使女以礼周流无不遍也。”子贡越席而对曰：“敢问何如？”子曰：“敬而不中礼，谓之野；恭而不中礼，谓之给；勇而不中礼，谓之逆。”子曰：“给夺慈仁。”子曰：“师，尔过；而商也不及。子产犹众人之母也，能食之不能教也。”子贡越席而对曰：“敢问将何以为此中者也？”子曰：“礼乎礼！夫礼所以制中也。”
子贡退，言游进曰：“敢问礼也者，领恶而全好者与？”子曰：“然。”“然则何如？”子曰：“郊社之义，所以仁鬼神也；尝禘之礼，所以仁昭穆也；馈奠之礼，所以仁死丧也；射乡之礼，所以仁乡党也；食飨之礼，所以仁宾客也。”子曰：“明乎郊社之义、尝禘之礼，治国其如指诸掌而已乎！是故，以之居处有礼，故长幼辨也。以之闺门之内有礼，故三族和也。以之朝廷有礼，故官爵序也。以之田猎有礼，故戎事闲也。以之军旅有礼，故武功成也。是故，宫室得其度，量鼎得其象，味得其时，乐得其节，车得其式，鬼神得其飨，丧纪得其哀，辨说得其党，官得其体，政事得其施；加于身而错于前，凡众之动得其宜。”
子曰：“礼者何也？即事之治也。君子有其事，必有其治。治国而无礼，譬犹瞽之无相与？伥伥其何之？譬如终夜有求于幽室之中，非烛何见？若无礼则手足无所错，耳目无所加，进退揖让无所制。是故，以之居处，长幼失其别；闺门，三族失其和；朝廷，官爵失其序；田猎，戎事失其策；军旅，武功失其制；宫室，失其度；量鼎，失其象；味，失其时；乐，失其节；车，失其式；鬼神，失其飨；丧纪，失其哀；辩说，失其党；官，失其体；政事，失其施；加于身而错于前，凡众之动，失其宜。如此，则无以祖洽于众也。”
……
en:
【Confucius at Leisure, Chapter 28】

Confucius was at leisure, and Zizhang, Zigong, and Yanyou were in attendance. As they conversed freely, the discussion turned to ritual. The Master said, "Sit down! You three, I will teach you about ritual, so that you may practice it everywhere without omission." Zigong stepped across his mat and replied, "May I ask what it is like?" The Master said, "Respect that does not accord with ritual is called boorishness; deference that does not accord with ritual is called glibness; courage that does not accord with ritual is called defiance." The Master said, "Glibness robs one of kindness and benevolence." The Master said, "Shi, you go too far; but Shang does not go far enough. Zichan was like a mother to the common people—he could feed them but could not teach them." Zigong stepped across his mat and replied, "May I ask how one may achieve this mean?" The Master said, "Ritual, indeed ritual! It is ritual that regulates the mean."
Zigong withdrew, and Yanyou stepped forward and said, "May I ask whether ritual is that which restrains what is evil and preserves what is good?" The Master said, "Yes." "Then how is this accomplished?" The Master said, "The meaning of the suburban and altar sacrifices is to show benevolence to the spirits; the rites of the chang and di sacrifices are to show benevolence to the ancestral order; the rites of offerings and oblations are to show benevolence to the dead; the rites of archery and the district drinking ceremony are to show benevolence to one's community; the rites of feasting and banqueting are to show benevolence to guests." The Master said, "If one understands the meaning of the suburban and altar sacrifices and the rites of the chang and di sacrifices, governing a state would be as easy as pointing to one's palm! Therefore, when ritual is observed in daily life, the distinctions between old and young are made clear. When ritual is observed within the household, the three clans live in harmony. When ritual is observed at court, official ranks are properly ordered. When ritual is observed in hunting, military affairs are well practiced. When ritual is observed in the army, martial achievements are accomplished. Thus, palaces and chambers attain their proper measure, measures and tripods attain their proper forms, flavors attain their proper seasons, music attains its proper moderation, carriages attain their proper standards, spirits and deities receive their proper offerings, mourning rites attain their proper grief, arguments attain their proper company, officials attain their proper roles, and government affairs attain their proper execution. When ritual is applied to oneself and set before one, all actions of the multitude attain their proper fitness."
The Master said, "What is ritual? It is the management of affairs. A gentleman, having affairs, must have proper management. To govern a state without ritual is like a blind man without a guide—where, bewildered, could he go? It is like searching all night in a dark chamber—without a lamp, how could one see? Without ritual, hands and feet have nowhere to be placed, ears and eyes have nothing to attend to, and advancing, retreating, bowing, and yielding have no regulation. Therefore, when ritual is lacking in daily life, the distinctions between old and young are lost; in the household, the three clans lose their harmony; at court, official ranks lose their order; in hunting, military affairs lose their strategy; in the army, martial achievements lose their control; palaces and chambers lose their proper measure; measures and tripods lose their proper forms; flavors lose their proper seasons; music loses its moderation; carriages lose their standards; spirits and deities lose their offerings; mourning rites lose their grief; arguments lose their proper company; officials lose their roles; and government affairs lose their execution. When ritual is applied to oneself and set before one, all actions of the multitude lose their fitness. In such a case, there is no way to lead and unite the people."
……

zh: 此唐人手写卷子谱《碣石调·幽兰》（第五），相传为孔子所作，传自南朝梁代隐士丘明，是现存最早的琴曲谱。曲子共分四段，通过描绘兰花的品格表达了虽不被重用，但并不颓丧的感情。该谱保持了早期文字谱的记写方式，共二百二十四行（每行二十至二十四字不等），四千九百五十四字，现藏于东京国立博物馆，编号为TB1393。
en: This Tang Dynasty manuscript score titled Jieshi Tune - Solitary Orchid (Vol. 5), traditionally attributed to Confucius and transmitted by the Liang Dynasty hermit Qiu Ming, stands as the oldest surviving score in existence. The piece is divided into four sections, conveying through its portrayal of the orchid's noble character a sentiment of remaining undefeated in spirit despite unrecognized talent. The score preserves the early character-based notation system, comprising 224 lines (with 20-24 characters per line) and totaling 4,954 characters. Currently housed at the Tokyo National Museum under No. TB1393.

群策共有#Y三人/四人/五人#E三种模式，少侠可以直接匹配或组成队伍进行匹配，三种模式均为#Y3局2胜制#E，共享积分段位。

「第一局」特殊2v2：
每队需要#Y2名#E玩家上阵，分别进行#Y1v1#E比赛，若2场比赛获胜者来自同一队伍，则该队伍获得第一局胜利；若2场比赛获胜者来自不同队伍，则2名胜者需以#Y当前状态#E进行对决，获胜方队伍获得第一局胜利；若1v1比赛倒计时结束时有未分出胜负的比赛，则场上所有幸存玩家需以当前状态进行对决，获胜方队伍获得第一局胜利

「第二局」3v3/5v5
三人/四人模式下，每队需要#Y3名#E玩家准备，进行#Y3v3#E比赛，获胜方队伍获得第二局胜利
五人模式下，每队需要#Y5名#E玩家准备，进行#Y5v5#E比赛，获胜方队伍获得第二局胜利

「第三局」1v1
每队需要#Y1名#E玩家准备，进行#Y1v1#E比赛，该玩家与第一局的2名玩家#Y不能重复#E

群策玩法中少侠的战斗属性将进行部分调平（角色自身装备套装/调律/定音效果生效；真气、精元、耐力均为满值，武学等级为100级，奇术为六重45段，心法为六重，止戈天赋除自选属性外全部点亮。食物和符帖效果在玩法中不生效。其中若少侠已经领悟奇术变招，则对局中的奇术效果将与对局外设置保持一致；若尚未领悟，则可在奇术培养界面设置是否试用奇术变招。）。少侠可以直接匹配或组队进行匹配。群策第一、三场对局中，玩家造成的治疗效果将降低70%，对目标的气血护盾造成的伤害提升100%，箭矢使用上限为20支，进入战斗一段时间后，玩家伤害将获得提升。群策第二场对局中，少侠可以复活队友，但玩家造成的治疗效果将降低70%。箭矢使用上限为20支。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。玩法中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。解控技能清风霁月可在受击或控制状态下使用，活用可以有效扭转劣势。

移动端与PC端为独立的匹配池。组队参与玩法时，匹配逻辑遵循以下规则：系统将检测队伍内所有成员的设备类型。一旦检测到存在PC端设备，该队伍会被纳入PC端匹配队列。若玩家在移动端匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方全部玩家的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
There are three modes in Group Strategy: #Y3-player, 4-player, and 5-player#E. Match directly or form a team. Ranks and Rank Points are shared across all three modes, and they all follow a #Ybest-of-3#E.

[Round 1] Special 2v2:
Each Team sends #Y2#E Players into battle to compete in two separate #Y1v1#E matches. If both members of a team win their individual matches, that team wins Round 1. If the winners belong to different teams, the 2 winners must duel in their #Ycurrent status#E, and the team of the victorious player claims Round 1. If any 1v1 match remains undecided when the time expires, all surviving players on the field must duel in their current status, and the team that wins claims Round 1.

[Round 2] 3v3/5v5
In 3-player/4-player Mode, each team must send #Y3#E players for a #Y3v3#E match. The team that wins claims Round 2.
In 5-player Mode, each team must send #Y5#E players for a #Y5v5#E match. The team that wins claims Round 2.

[Round 3] 1v1
Each Team must send #Y1#E player for a #Y1v1#E match. This player #Ycannot be#E one of the two players from Round 1.

In Group Strategy, Combat Attributes will be partially adjusted (Character's Gear Set/Tune/Attunement effects remain active; Qi, Vitality, and Endurance are set to max values, Martial Art Level is set to Lv. 100, Mystic Skill is set to 6th Circle Stage 45, Inner Way is set to 6th Circle, and all Arena Talents except self-selected Attributes will be fully activated. Food and Scroll & Script cannot be used. If the player has already comprehended Mystic Skill Variants, no changes will be made to the Skill effects in-match. Otherwise, you may choose trial Mystic Skill Variants in the Mystic Skill Develop Interface.) You may match directly or form a team. In Group Strategy Rounds 1 and 3, healing effects are reduced by 70%, damage to HP Shield is increased by 100%, Arrow usage is capped at 20, and damage dealt is increased over time upon entering battle. In Group Strategy Round 2, you will be able to revive teammates, but healing effects are reduced by 70%. Additionally, Arrow usage is capped at 20.

Most skills can be countered with Deflect. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills cannot be deflected; they deal enhanced damage to targets using Defense or Deflect, but can be interrupted by any skill. Using Deflect costs Endurance, while landing an Execution restores it.

Player skills (including Mystic and Charged) can interrupt Light/Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. Use Break Control Skills like Serene Breeze to escape control effects and turn the tide.

Mobile and PC players queue separately. In team queue, if any member is using a PC, the entire team enters the PC matchmaking pool. Players showing abnormal cross-platform behavior (e.g., account takeover) on mobile will be moved to the PC queue.

Win by eliminating all opponents. If time expires, victory is decided by:
1) Surviving players, 2) Total damage, 3) Total healing.

zh:

这可不行，爹娘知道了要骂。
从那天开始，村里谁屋顶的瓦坏了，第二天也就自己好了。谁的摊子又给江湖人打散了，过几天也就恢复原样了。
村里的人都啧啧称奇，杜乾拿着手上的钱唉声叹气。
还是花不完，怎么办呢？他眼睛一转，当天晚上小妹妹房里就多了一个插满糖葫芦的架子。
第一日，小妹妹拉着他笑得很开心。
第十日，小妹妹因为蛀牙疼哭了。
杜乾很心疼，他管这叫好心办坏事。他当下决定，把赌棋摊再开大些，吆喝再用力些，把这些钱都给小妹妹治牙病。
杜乾又有动力赚钱了。
果然，给小妹妹花钱，才能持续不断地花。杜乾摸摸下巴：可算给我找到持续花钱的正道了！
en:
The coins piled up quickly. Too quickly, in fact, he soon found he had no idea how to spend them. After much thought, he realized what was missing... He'd done plenty of "taking from the rich," but had forgotten about "helping the poor."
That wouldn't do. His parents would scold him if they knew.
From then on, odd things began to happen around the village. A broken roof tile would fix itself overnight. A stall smashed up by rough wanderers would be back in business a few days later.
The villagers whispered in wonder. Du Qian, meanwhile, stared at his purse and sighed.
He still had too much money. What now? Suddenly, inspiration struck. That night, a rack bristling with candied hawthorn appeared in the little girl's room.
On the first day, she was happy and smiled a lot at him.
By the tenth, she was crying from a toothache.
Du Qian was heartbroken. His kind intention had gone horribly wrong. On the spot, he made a new plan: make the gambling stall bigger, shout louder, earn more, and spend it all getting her teeth fixed.
Du Qian had his motivation back.
Sure enough, when the money was spent on someone he cared about, it finally began to disappear at a satisfying pace. Du Qian rubbed his chin, pleased. So this was the right way to spend money!

zh:
一路上，每逢雨夜，陈霖便会想起那天......
客栈的灯火被雨丝晕开，姑娘收拢的伞尖滴着水，静静地将一个钱袋推到桌前。
他抬着眼皮敲了一眼，那袋子还没平日他栓在腰上的酒壶大。
“不够！”，他不耐烦地说完，正打算低头继续理账本，却听见那姑娘背后的声音传来——
“我们补上！”他抬眼，只见在灯火照不透的阴影里，站着密密麻麻一群人。
胡琴的轮廓，琵琶的弧光，还有卸不净的油彩，在光下若隐若现。珠钗碎银被一一放在桌上，叮当作响，如落雨入潭。
“我不懂。”他看着桌上越堆越高的光亮，“北边的仗，皇帝都不急，和你们这方戏台，更是隔着山水万里，你们管什么闲事？”
那姑娘迎着他的目光，声音不大，却砸得他心口一震：”我们不懂朝堂，只认一个理。当年天下人噤声，是王将军他们，在北边硬生生把脊梁骨挺直了，给全天下唱了出硬戏！”
“那不是闲事，”旁边的汉子闷声道，“那是台柱子。台柱子倒了，谁都得被砸死。”
陈霖没再说话，只是伸出手将那本写满算计的账本合上，
“钱既到位，这一单我接了！”
en:
On every rainy night along the road, Chen Lin is reminded of that day...
Rain blurred the lamplight at the inn. Water dripped from the tip of the girl's closed umbrella as she quietly pushed a pouch of coins onto the table. He barely glanced at it. The pouch was smaller than the wine flask at his waist.
"Not enough," he said impatiently, lowering his head back to his ledgers... until a voice came from behind her: "We'll make up the rest."
He looked up. A crowd stood in the shadows, untouched by the light. In the dim glow, he caught the outlines of erhus and pipas, traces of stage paint still clinging to their faces. One by one, jeweled hairpins and pieces of silver were set upon the table, their soft clinks like raindrops falling into a pond.
"I don't get it," he muttered, eyeing the growing pile of silver. "Even the Emperor couldn't care less about the war up north. It's a thousand miles away from your little stage. Why stick your noses in?"
The girl met his gaze, her voice quiet but striking deep: "We know nothing of the court, only this. When all under heaven fell silent, it was General Wang and his men who stood firm in the north, showing the world what resolve truly means."
"That's no idle matter," the man beside her said in a low voice. "They are the pillars that hold us all up. If they fall, none of us will stand."
Chen Lin said nothing more. He reached out and closed the ledger filled with calculations: "The money's there. I'll take the job."

zh:
廉道子有一个绝招，这个绝招可以帮他应对世上九成九的事。这绝招只有一个字——“好”。 
父亲好，继母好，弟弟好，搬家好，换屋子好，不说汉话也还好。家中狸奴闹起来委实恼人，丢了也好。破了洞的衣服没人补正好，总是要换身衣服的嘛。碗里的绿豆酥比弟弟少一个也好，他又不爱吃甜。每日少读一个时辰的书去接弟弟回家则是太好了，反正也不想跟着夫子念那劳什子经。冬至祭灶和拜祠堂的人换成了弟弟……好吧，谁早上爱起来谁起，反正他是不起。好的多了，他的好就变成像日头升起一样的每日惯例。他有一个挺漂亮的旧琵琶，是祖父给他的。他不会弹成段的曲子，但总是抱着。或许是琵琶轴太紧或者太旧，他抱着琵琶时，琵琶有时候会“吱呀吱呀”的喊他，他就“好呀好呀”的应和。他和琵琶挺好的，所以一切都还好。父亲倒是说过不好，说他站没站相吊儿郎当无所谓做什么都好好好，不像个男儿样子。他耸耸肩，回了个“好”，扭头走了。 
直到一日，他回到家，发现他的琵琶正被搬上商人的马车。他冲过去抢下琵琶，嘴唇颤抖，一个字都说不出来。弟弟倒是拍着手叫起好来，继母也劝他那琵琶他又不弹，放在家里都要放坏了，卖些银钱不好吗？父亲倒是一如既往的横眉怒目，一巴掌甩在他脸上，让他好好看看自己现在这副样子，要么把琵琶放下，要么滚出这个家。 
琵琶委屈地躲在他怀里，吱呀吱呀地向他告状。好先生，好好先生，不要说那个字…… 
他抬起头，阳光刺眼。 
“好。”
en:
Lian Daozi had a master move, one that could help him deal with ninety-nine percent of the world's matters. This master move consisted of a single word, "Fine."  
Father, fine. Stepmother, fine. Younger brother, fine. Moving house, fine. Changing rooms, fine. Not speaking Han language, also fine. The house cat causing trouble was truly annoying, losing it was fine too. Clothes with holes, no one to mend them, just fine, one always needs to change clothes anyway. Having one less mung bean pastry in his bowl than his brother, fine, he didn't like sweets anyway. Reading one less hour of books each day to pick up his brother from school was just wonderful, he didn't want to recite that bothersome Confucian text with the teacher anyway. Younger brother taking over the Winter Solstice stove offering and ancestral hall worship... fine, whoever wants to get up in the morning can get up, he certainly wasn't going to. After enough "fines," his agreeableness became a daily routine, as regular as the sun rising. He had a rather beautiful old pipa, given by his grandfather. He couldn't play complete melodies, but he always held it. Perhaps the tuning pegs were too tight or too old, when he held the pipa, it would sometimes creak and call to him, and he would respond, "Fine, fine." He and the pipa got along fine, so everything was still fine. Father did once say it wasn't fine, that he stood without posture, was sloppy, indifferent, said "fine" to everything, not manly at all. He shrugged, replied "Fine," and turned away.  
Until one day, he returned home to find his pipa being loaded onto a merchant's cart. He rushed over, snatched back the pipa, his lips trembling, unable to utter a single word. His younger brother, however, clapped and cheered, while his stepmother urged him, saying he didn't play it anyway, it would just rot at home, wouldn't getting some silver for it be better? His father, as ever, scowled with anger, slapped him across the face, told him to take a good look at himself now, and to either put the pipa down or get out of this house.  
The pipa, aggrieved, nestled in his embrace, creaking and complaining to him. Mr. Agreeable, good Mr. Agreeable, don't say that word...  
He looked up. The sunlight was blinding.  
"Okay."

创建房间：
玩家可自由创建砺兵台房间，创房成功后会自动成为房主，拥有该房间内成员管理权与出战安排权限。房主可以向房间内其他成员转让房主身份，若房主直接退出则会自动把房主权限转让给房间内人气值最高的成员。

赛制：
房主可设置该房间的挑战模式，分为自由模式和管理模式。
自由模式下，房间内玩家可自由选择场内成员或队伍发起叫阵或指名挑战；
管理模式下，房间内玩家或队长报名后，由房主决定对战双方；
胜负判定分为三种：一局一胜、三局两胜和五局三胜；
砺兵台目前仅支持1V1模式。

人气值及房间热度：
在房间内收到赠礼会增加个人的人气值。房间内人数越多、战斗次数和赠礼次数越多，房间的热度值越高。@T[time_5]会重新计算各房间的热度及房间内各成员的人气值。
en:
Create Room:
Players can create Training Terrace rooms and become the Host, managing members and matches. Ownership can be transferred or automatically passed to the most popular member if the Host leaves.

Formats:
The Host can set the Challenge Mode: Free Mode or Management Mode.
Free Mode: Players can freely select opponents or teams to issue Challenges or Targeted Duels.
Management Mode: Players or Captains sign up, and the Host decides the match-ups.
Victory Conditions: Best of 1, Best of 3, or Best of 5.
Training Terrace supports 1v1 battles.

Popularity and Room Heat:
Receiving gifts increases personal Popularity. More members, battles, and gifts increase Room Popularity. Both reset daily at @T[time_5].

zh:
【卫灵公第十五】

卫灵公问陈于孔子。孔子对曰：“俎豆之事，则尝闻之矣。军旅之事，未之学也。”明日遂行。
在陈绝粮，从者病，莫能兴。子路愠见曰：“君子亦穷乎？”子曰：“君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣。”
子曰：“赐也，汝以予为多学而识之者与？”对曰：“然。非与？”曰：“非也，予一以贯之。”
子曰：“由，知德者鲜矣。”
子曰：“无为而治者，其舜也与！夫何为哉？恭己正南面而己矣。”
子张问行。子曰：“言忠信，行笃敬，虽蛮㹮之邦，行矣。言不忠信，行不笃敬，虽州里，行乎哉！立，则见其参然于前也，在舆则见其倚于衡也，夫然后行也。”子张书诸绅。
子曰：“直哉史鱼！邦有道，如矢；邦无道，如矢。君子哉，蘧伯玉！邦有道，则仕；邦无道，则可卷而怀也。”
子曰：“可与言而不与言，失人；不可与言而与言之，失言。知者不失人，亦不失言。”
子曰：“志士仁人，无求生以害仁，有杀身以成仁。”
子贡问为仁。子曰：“工欲善其事，必先利其器。居是邦也，事其大夫之贤者，友其士之仁者也。”
颜渊问为邦。子曰：“行夏之时，乘殷之辂，服周之冕，乐则韶舞，放郑声，远佞人。郑声淫，佞人殆。”
子曰：“人而无远虑，必有近忧。”
子曰：“已矣乎，吾未见好德如好色者也。”
子曰：“臧文仲其窃位者与？知柳下惠之贤，而不与立也。”
子曰：“躬自厚而薄责于人，则远怨矣。”
子曰：“不曰如之何，如之何者，吾末如之何也已矣。”
……
en:
Book 15: Duke Ling of Wei

Duke Ling of Wei asked Confucius about military formations. Confucius replied, "I have heard about sacrificial vessels, but I have not studied military matters." The next day, he departed.
In the state of Chen, their provisions ran out, and his followers fell ill, unable to rise. Zilu, looking resentful, said, "Does a gentleman also face hardship?" Confucius said, "A gentleman remains steadfast in hardship; a petty man, when in hardship, becomes reckless."
Confucius said, "Ci, do you think I am one who learns much and remembers it all?" Zigong replied, "Yes. Is that not so?" Confucius said, "No. I have one thread that runs through it all."
Confucius said, "You, there are few who understand virtue."
Confucius said, "He who governed without action—was it not Shun? What did he do? He simply made himself reverent and faced south correctly."
Zizhang asked about conduct. Confucius said, "Be loyal and trustworthy in speech, earnest and respectful in action. Even among barbarian tribes, you will succeed. If speech is not loyal and trustworthy, action not earnest and respectful, even in your own district, will you succeed? When standing, see these principles before you; in the carriage, see them resting on the crossbar. Only then will you succeed." Zizhang wrote this on his sash.
Confucius said, "How upright was Shi Yu! When the state was well-ordered, he was like an arrow; when the state lacked the Way, he was like an arrow. A true gentleman, Qu Boyu! When the state was well-ordered, he served; when the state lacked the Way, he could withdraw and keep his principles to himself."
Confucius said, "To fail to speak with someone you can speak to is to lose the person. To speak with someone you cannot speak to is to waste words. The wise lose neither the person nor waste words."
Confucius said, "A determined scholar or a man of benevolence does not seek life at the expense of benevolence; there are those who would sacrifice their lives to achieve benevolence."
Zigong asked about practicing benevolence. Confucius said, "A craftsman who wishes to do his work well must first sharpen his tools. When residing in a state, serve the worthy among its great officers and befriend the benevolent among its scholars."
Yan Yuan asked about governing a state. Confucius said, "Follow the calendar of Xia, ride in the carriage of Yin, wear the ceremonial cap of Zhou, and for music, adopt the Shao dance. Banish the tunes of Zheng and keep flatterers at a distance. The tunes of Zheng are licentious; flatterers are dangerous."
Confucius said, "If a man takes no thought for what is distant, he will find sorrow near at hand."
Confucius said, "It is all over! I have never seen one who loves virtue as he loves beauty."
Confucius said, "Was Zang Wenzhong one who stole his position? He knew the worth of Liu Xiahui but did not stand by him."
Confucius said, "Be strict with yourself and lenient with others, and you will keep resentment at a distance."
Confucius said, "If a man does not say, 'What is to be done? What is to be done?' I can do nothing with him."
...
Put Down the Wine Jar
— Mathematical Classic for Beginners, by Xie Chawei, Song Dynasty

在那牙尖嘴利的狗崽子惊讶的目光里，这一刀，他调转了刀背。
运气不错，他认出了这手稚嫩的令人发笑的刀法。
——寒香寻那女人也不是个省油的灯，怎么养个孩子这般天真？
这小崽子，倒认识不少人。留着比杀了有用。
只是，少不得还是要教训一通，好叫这天真崽子知道，江湖险恶。
他收起紫金大刀。
“喂，狗崽子，带老子去不羡仙。”

带个路而已，那么多心眼子。
趁他去探路，这小崽子果然不老实地溜之大吉。
他伊刀说话，一口唾沫一口钉，说不杀人，就不杀人。
竟还不信——这么怕他找寒香寻那臭女人的麻烦不成！
不过，毛都没长齐的小崽子，就算有点小聪明，哪里斗得过他老江湖客——
浓雾中，伊刀装模作样地喊了几句，便大摇大摆地跟上了前方慌乱逃离的身影。
也不想想，若不是他故意，谁能从他死人刀手中逃脱！
得意地一笑。
小崽子，跑吧！你跑得越快，就把你寒姨出卖得越多！
en:
The first time Yi Dao met the little one of Han Xiangxun, he scoffed. 
Where did this clueless kid come from? 
Not only did the kid not run when he saw the infamous Killerblade, but he even dared to draw his own sword. 
Gutsy, Yi Dao thought. But let's see how long those guts last against a few of my swings. 
They fought, with blade against blade. The kid was no match for him, but when Yi Dao struck, there was no blood. 
The kid stared at him in shock. Yi Dao had used the back of his blade. 
He realized then that this laughably clumsy swordplay was familiar. 
So Han Xiangxun raised a kid this naive? She was never an easy one herself. 
The kid seemed to know all sorts of people. The kid might be more useful alive than dead. 
Still, he needed to teach the kid a lesson that Jianghu was a dangerous place. 
Yi Dao sheathed his blade. 
"Hey, take me to Blissful Retreat." 

Just showing the way, there is no need to be so cagey about it. 
As soon as he went ahead to scout, the little kid predictably slipped away at the first chance. 
Yi Dao always kept his word. If he said he wouldn't kill, then he wouldn't kill. 
And yet, the kid still didn't trust him. Did he really think Yi Dao would go looking for trouble with Han Xiangxun, that troublesome woman? 
But honestly, a kid who's barely out of childhood, even with some wits, was no match for a seasoned old hand like Yi Dao. 
In the thick fog, Yi Dao called out half-heartedly, then swaggered after the panicked, fleeing figure ahead. 
Seriously, as if anyone could escape the Killerblade unless he let them! 
He couldn't help but grin smugly. 
Run, kid, run! The faster you go, the more you're giving your Aunt Han away!

夺我笔，犹有篆刀！当以刃为史笔，遍刻梁王之罪于秦川碑阴。

en:
Zhu Wen the traitor stormed my sect, intent on seizing the Ten Sages' Collection. My brethren gave their lives to defend it, their blood staining every stone step. That wound is carved into my soul. I will never forget it.

Now my disciples and I are kept as captives, forced to labor as stonemasons, carving merit steles for the very men who destroyed us. Each time I am made to remember, the will to die rises in me like a tide. Yet if I die now, their atrocities die with me. And so I endure. I swallow the shame and stay alive.

They have taken my brush. But my carving knife remains. Let steel serve as ink. I will inscribe the Prince of Liang's crimes into the stones of Qinchuan, into the incised backs of every stele they make us carve. Let the wind and rain wear them down. Let the years pass. Long after my bones are dust, the truth beneath my blade will come to light.

自鹿食林东北行数十里，过鹿潭，又四五里，至清河与开封交界，有狭道倚山壁蜿蜒而上，有馆隐于山中，曰“春秋别馆”，传为先朝贵人避暑旧地，自国朝更迭，荒废至今。
循阶而行，山皆石骨，拥峦夹翠，飞瀑自上而泄，下聚成潭，涉目成赏。又有飞檐翘角，隐于林木，虽久未修缮，屋舍大半完好。至馆门前，有壮士阻之，言此路不通，故返。返时隐闻瀑后有金石之声，怪矣。
en:
Traveling northeast from Deerforage Grove for tens of miles, past Deer Pond, and another four or five miles, one reaches the border of Qinghe and Kaifeng. Here, a narrow path hugs the mountain wall and winds upward, hiding a pavilion in the hills called the Palace of Annals. Legend has it that this was once a summer resort for nobles of the previous dynasty, but since the dynastic change, it has lain in ruins ever since. 
Following the stone steps, the mountains reveal their bony rock faces, embracing emerald valleys. A waterfall cascades down from above, gathering into a pool below—every view is a feast for the eyes. Upturned eaves peek through the trees, and though long unrepaired, most structures remain intact.
At the pavilion gate, a burly guard blocked the way, claiming the path was closed. As we turned back, a faint clinking of metal and stone echoed from behind the waterfall—strange indeed.

zh:
武威山的风是冷的，雪是甜的，梅花是涩的。张淮深都尝过。
他最爱独行策马登高。山巅风烈，眯眼望去，凉州城不过掌心大小。
友人邀他“禄伯，何时同看山？”
“下月。”
下月哪日？那对他和友人倒不重要。兴致来时，他便随手披上大氅——这些年不知丢了多少件，醉后扔在山间的，与人斗剑破的，雪地里裹了发抖的老翁的。
怀中揣上满江红，若至山顶并未见故人，便自斟一杯，或慰业已离去的朋友，或敬尚未来此的知交。
临行前，恰逢小小的风波。幼弟淮鼎扑来抱住张淮深的腿，缠他不许他走。
那便同去。他大笑着将小郎君拎上马背，白马嘶鸣，震落枝头积雪。
凉州人都记得他。少有人的马这样的快，耳力又这般的好。
张淮深耳力的确很好。月姊的赌咒，淮鼎的撒娇，农人的烦恼，张球的吟哦，索靖的琴声，雪夜里老翁的呼救，他全都听得真切。
夜不脱载的人也渐渐多了，怀月淮鼎索靖老翁张球，还有萍水相逢的知交。份量叠在鞍上，却未曾令他稍缓马速。白马越跑越快，快得幼弟的惊呼都碎在风里。
四野景色模糊，有呼喊不知来自怀中还是身后，忽远忽近似在追挽，张淮深懒得分辨。
“阿兄慢些！”
“得再快些。”
少年人的快马，世间有谁能拦？一团决意要轰烈燃尽，连余灰都不肯留的火，世间有谁能灭？
“去哪？”
“赴约。”
“和谁？”
他笑着扬鞭，指向漫天风雪。
en:
The wind on Wuwei Mountain is cold, the snow is sweet, and the plum blossoms are astringent. Zhang Huaishen has tasted them all. 
He loves riding alone to the heights. The wind is fierce at the mountain top, squinting his eyes, Liangzhou City looks no bigger than the palm of his hand. 
A friend once invited him: "Lubo, when shall we view the mountains together?" 
"Next month." 
Which day next month? It didn't matter much to him or his friend. When the mood struck, he would casually throw on a fur coat, over the years, he had lost countless ones, left in the mountains after getting drunk, torn during sword fights with others, or given to shivering old men in the snow. 
He would carry a flask of River All Red in his arms. If he didn't meet his old friend at the top, he would pour himself a drink, to comfort friends who had already left, or to toast bosom friends who had not yet come. 
Before he set off, a little incident happened. His young brother Huaiding rushed over, hugged Zhang Huaishen's legs, and pestered him to stay. 
So he took him along. Laughing loudly, he lifted the young boy onto the horseback. The white horse neighed, shaking the snow off the branches. 
Everyone in Liangzhou remembered him. Few people had such a fast horse, or such sharp hearing. 
Zhang Huaishen's hearing was indeed excellent. The oaths of Sister Yue, Huaiding's coquetry, the worries of farmers, Zhang Qiu's recitations, Suo Jing's qin playing, and the cries for help from old men on snowy nights, he heard them all clearly. 
Gradually, more and more people became constant companions on his journeys: Huaiyue, Huaiding, Suo Jing, the old man, Zhang Qiu, and even bosom friends met by chance. Their weight piled up on the saddle, yet it never slowed his horse down. The white horse ran faster and faster, so fast that his young brother's exclamations were shattered by the wind. 
The scenery blurred all around. Shouts came, whether from within his embrace or behind him, now distant, now near, as if chasing or pleading, Zhang Huaishen could not be bothered to tell. 
"Brother, slow down!" 
"We need to go faster." 
Who in the world can stop a young man's fast horse? Who can put out a fire that is determined to burn brightly to the end, leaving not even ashes behind? 
"Where are we going?" 
"To keep an appointment." 
"With whom?" 
He smiled, raised his whip, and pointed toward the snowstorm covering the sky.
