zh:
青州一带，山精野怪多，淫祠野祀亦多。泰山上多有子不语之事，九幽石刻，镇邪祟冤魂；厉鬼索命，客店死尸无数；夜道行客，困死山中，成失路之鬼……
注：荒谬荒谬。这般说来，此方地界怕是魑魅魍魉横行，难有我等生人落脚之处。
……
传早悟寺水泊畔、密林中，常有精怪，窃食贡枣，污毁佛像。所谓精怪，大抵是林中成群獐类。当吟诗一首：“獐怪獐怪，无食我枣。三岁贯汝，无害我佛。”
注：早悟寺西佛殿、北道观、南祠堂格局，虽为馆中师兄所倡，然至今路过，我仍以为奇。
……
至乐安浦，往来渔户皆供奉海神娘娘。传说海神娘娘与龙王共司东海，龙王性暴虐，喜以风暴席卷舟楫；海神娘娘性至善，常驾小舟出入风涛，救溺者无数。可若是神明，何故驭舟？想来不过是善掌舵的女子，屡屡救人，以讹传讹便成神异。
今遍听渔家舟子口述，记录如下几则异闻：
青州有贾舟泊蓬莱湾，樯摧楫折，危在顷刻。众伏舟中惶惧，祷于神，忽见火发桅杪，光如朗月，前导而行。须臾浪平，遥见一彩衣女子立波上，手执红灯，徐徐入云而去。
乐安浦有渔者张旺，夜舟遇飓，浪高丈余，昏黑不辨东西。一船惶怖，伏舱呼神。俄见桅杪悬红灯，引舟前行，浪随灯低，水为之分。至晓已泊黄河滩。旺悟曰：“昨夜非神人显灵，吾辈皆鱼腹矣！”
蓬莱渔者王顺，妻病笃，祷于海神。夜梦彩衣女子，授青囊一丸，曰：“以水调服，可愈。”旦果见案上遗丸，妻服之，疾瘳。
……
昨夜我独驾小舟，往海上观潮。未及半程，天色骤变，海风呼啸，浪起丈余。昏黑之中难辨东西，唯闻涛声如雷，心中惶惧，想我此生洒脱不羁，莫非将命丧于此？
忽见前方有红灯一盏，悬于桅杪。我驾驭舟楫，追索灯影而去，不知行了几许，但觉风渐平，浪渐息。及至天明，舟已泊于乐安浦。举目四望，红灯已杳，四顾无人。
登岸问于渔者，皆说是海神娘娘引路。我素不信鬼神，然昨夜之事，历历在目。若无人引，何以脱险？若非神助，何以不见其形？
注：我反复思量，疑心所谓海神娘娘，或许是往来渔舟见有船遇险，悬灯引之，救毕即去，不告姓名。一人如此，众人亦如此，积年累月，口耳相传，便成神异。
渔家终日与风涛为伍，生死悬于一线，若无一念之寄，恐难撑持。海神娘娘之信仰，或正是此念之化身。
……
今追思前事，始觉昔日论断未免轻率。泰山九幽石刻，本为镇邪之物，然石壁危悬，观者不慎则坠。有人子见石刻古奥，攀援而窥，失足堕崖。其父遂每晨负绳携水，巡行山径，见游人将堕则呼而止之。凡二十载，所救不下百人。他日或有渔樵相传，谓山有神人，夜游于危崖，救度失路之鬼，亦未可知。
早悟寺獐怪窃枣之事，余尝亲见。后闻老僧言：“十数年前，山中大雪，群獐无食，入寺求乞。先师悯之，取贡枣饲。岁以为常，獐亦渐不畏人。”
余向者以理度物，见神异辄曰“此乃讹传”，自以为智，实非怠邪？不可不可，自当改之。
记于显德三年四月廿六
en:
In the region of Qingzhou, mountain spirits and wild monsters are abundant, as are uncanonical shrines and rustic cults. On Mount Tai, there are numerous matters of which the ancient Master did not speak: the Nine Hells Inscription suppressing evil spirits and wronged souls; malicious ghosts claiming lives, leaving countless corpses in inns; night travelers trapped in the mountains, becoming wandering specters of the lost...
Note: Absurd, utterly absurd. If one listens to such talk, this realm is overrun by demons and hobgoblins, leaving no place for the living to set foot.
...
It is rumored that by the waters and within the dense woods of Seedling Temple, woodland sprites frequently appear, stealing sacrificial dates and defiling the Buddha statues. These so-called sprites are likely just herds of roe deer from the forest. One should chant a poem: "Woodland sprites, woodland sprites, devour not my dates. Three years I have fed thee, harm not my Buddha."
Note: The layout of Seedling Temple, with a Buddhist hall to the west, a Daoist shrine to the north, and an ancestral hall to the south, was proposed by a senior brother from the Order. Yet, passing by it today, I still find it remarkably strange.
...
Arriving at Tranquil Pier, I noted that all the coming and going fisherfolk worship the Sea Goddess. Legend says she governs the Eastern Sea alongside the Dragon King. The Dragon King is cruel by nature, delighting in sweeping away boats with storms; the Matriarch, however, embodies supreme kindness, often sailing a small skiff through the wind and waves to save the drowning. But if she is a deity, why must she steer a boat? It is highly probable she was merely a mortal woman skilled at the helm who repeatedly saved lives, and through repeated embellishment, her deeds became divine legend.
Having listened to the accounts of the fishermen and boatmen, I record the following anomalies:
A merchant ship from Qingzhou moored at Penglai Bay. Its masts were shattered, its oars broken, and peril was imminent. The crew cowered in the cabin in terror, praying to the gods. Suddenly, a fire flared at the tip of the mast, glowing as bright as a clear moon, leading the way forward. In moments, the waves calmed. In the distance, they saw a woman in colorful robes standing upon the waves, holding a red lantern, slowly ascending into the clouds.
Zhang Wang, a fisherman of Tranquil Pier, encountered a hurricane at night. The waves towered over ten feet high, and the darkness obscured all directions. The entire boat was struck with terror, kneeling in the cabin to cry out to the gods. Soon, a red lantern was seen hanging from the mast, guiding the boat onward. The waves lowered where the lantern passed, and the waters parted. By dawn, they had moored at the shoals of the Yellow River. Wang suddenly realized: "Had the divine not manifested last night, we would all be in the bellies of fishes!"
...
Last night, I sailed a small boat alone to watch the tide at sea. Before I was halfway there, the sky suddenly changed, the sea winds howled, and the waves surged over ten feet. I could not distinguish direction in the pitch black, hearing only the thunderous roar of the tide. Fear gripped my heart. I, who have lived a life of unbridled freedom, thought I might meet my end here.
Suddenly, I saw a red lantern ahead, suspended at the mast's tip. I steered my boat, chasing the phantom of the light. I know not how far I traveled, but I felt the winds gradually calm and the waves subside. When dawn broke, the boat was already moored at Tranquil Pier. I looked around, but the red lantern had vanished, and there was no one in sight.
Going ashore to ask the fishermen, they all claimed it was the Sea Goddess guiding the way. I have never believed in ghosts or gods, yet the events of last night remain vivid in my mind. If no one guided me, how did I escape danger? If it was not divine aid, why was no figure seen?
Note: I have pondered this repeatedly. I suspect that the so-called Sea Goddess might simply be passing fishing boats that, upon seeing a vessel in distress, hang a lantern to guide it, and depart immediately after the rescue without leaving a name. One person does this, and others follow suit. Over the years, passed from mouth to ear, it becomes a divine myth. The fisherfolk spend their days battling wind and waves, their lives hanging by a thread. Without a sliver of faith to rely upon, they could hardly endure. The worship of the Sea Goddess is perhaps the very incarnation of this psychological anchor.
...
Recalling the past today, I begin to feel my previous judgments were too hasty. I used to measure the world strictly by logic; upon seeing anomalies, I would casually dismiss them as "false rumors," thinking myself wise. Was this not actually intellectual laziness? It will not do. I must correct this flaw.
Recorded on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month, the third year of Xiande.

zh:
谨肃具书。此生入文津馆以来，读书过目成诵，论道每有独见，历试辄拔其萃。诸生视之，如出群之鸾鹤，独秀之芝兰；然余观之，头痛之甚，每见其率性而行，不谙世故，未尝不抚额而叹。
此生性尚纯真，执拗难阻，易为佞人所诓。今其志有所向，别怀远略，欲投贵派。江湖险恶，邪僻之所在多有，非可信之托，不敢轻付。余素知贵派风规严正，足以陶铸真才，故敢修书为荐，兼以托付。伏望贵派俯允收录，毋负瑾瑜。
呜呼哀哉！天下师者，孰不愿徒子绕膝承欢？余亦人师，焉能外也？然此生去意如铁，志不可夺。我心忧伤，惄焉如捣，终不忍以区区师生之情，束其凌云之翼。愿此生于贵派学有所成，兼取两门之长，致用于世。如此，余虽失一朝夕伴学之生，天下可得一躬行大道之士。 
临书怅怅，忽忆此生初谒，彼时尚带三分草莽气，今已怀得七分圣贤心。昔日袖中或藏闲食、匿小抄，每为吾所叱咄；今当别离，倒不由再三叮嘱，袖中多备干粮，行路迢迢，莫叫腹空。
常归故馆，以慰旧怀。
 
文津馆不具名之师暨双元 合荐
en:
Respectfully submitted. Since entering the Inkbound Order, this student has proven brilliant, memorizing texts at a glance and excelling in every debate and exam. To their peers, they are a crane among chickens. Yet, to me, they are a massive headache: pure of heart, stubbornly impulsive, and utterly ignorant of the world's ways.
They are a prime target for silver-tongued scoundrels. Now, their ambitions lead them to your esteemed sect. Knowing your strict discipline and upright ethos, I take the liberty to recommend them, entrusting this unpolished gem to your care.
What teacher does not wish their disciples to remain? My heart aches, yet I will not use our bonds to shackle their soaring wings. May they combine the strengths of both our schools to become a righteous champion of the Great Way.
Finishing this letter, I am filled with melancholy, remembering when they first arrived with a trace of rustic wildness. In the past, they hid cheat sheets in their sleeves; now, as we part, I only find myself reminding them to pack extra rations in those same sleeves.
The journey is long. Return often to the pavilion to comfort our nostalgic hearts.
 
Co-recommended by: Twin Mavens & an anonymous teacher of the Inkbound Order

“什么心愿？”

#Y【弱女归家】——弱女归家，世间骨肉不必再分离。#E”
en:
As night fell, the lanterns of the Ghostlight Market rose again, as they had through countless turnings of day and night. Yet the wanderer who once recklessly stumbled into this place has not returned for a long, long time.
Lu wondered if the hero had gone off into the jianghu. Was the jianghu a fun place? And where exactly was it?
"Then let's go ask!" Fu cried out.
The three ran into the Ghostlight Market and asked Niu Tou. Niu Tou replied, "The jianghu? It's just a chaotic brawl of clashing sabers and swords."
Lu shook her head. That didn't sound like any fun at all.
Then they asked Granny Yin. Granny Yin said, "Why, this place right here is the jianghu."
Shou shook her head. "Here? Does the Ghostlight Market count as the jianghu?"
The Dao Lords went to the teahouse to listen to storytelling. Mr. Ghost was there again, telling of the great war with the Khitan, of Chief Zhu, and of the spectral soldiers of the Ghostlight Market.
The Dao Lords nodded. "Oh, right, we know that part. This really is the jianghu! But sir, aren't people of the jianghu always coming and going without a trace? Why have the spectral soldiers stayed here all this time?"
Mr. Ghost said, "Most likely, their final wishes remain unfulfilled."
"What wishes?"
Mr. Ghost replied, "Perhaps they never lived to see...

en: Erysipelas, or Heavenly Fire, it begins as red markings on the flesh, sometimes as large as a palm. Severe cases cover the body, causing itching and swelling with no fixed pattern. In White Dan, the flesh swells and itches with aching pain; the swelling feels airy, like wind trapped under skin. In Crest Dan, red bumps rise in clusters, as large as a chain of coins or as small as millet seeds, with a texture like a crest; also called Dogwood Dan. In Water Dan, heat spreads across the body and, when mingled with damp, forms pustules like water under the skin, shimmering yellow-red and often found on the thighs and groin. Though seemingly minor at onset, if left untreated, it may lead to death.

祀血问诛，古已有之。
凡历代巨子所为有污，有弟子坚心向背者，经长老见证，便可祀血问诛。
问诛者胜生败死，此性命之搏。
为巨子者，上承窥天之志，下继一派渊流。
若无舍身求道的决心，又如何当得这巨子的名头？
身继窥天之任，决心历来所重。
只是这一次，问诛的两人，
决心都一样炽热，一个向生，一个向死。
头也不回，就这样走到尽头。
en:
The Duel of Blood has existed since ancient times.
Whenever a Grandmaster's actions are deemed a stain upon the sect, any disciple steadfast enough to stand against them may, with the elders as witnesses, invoke the Duel of Blood.
In such a duel, the victor lives and the defeated dies. It is a struggle fought with one's life on the line.
A Grandmaster bears the will to peer into heaven above and carries forward the sect's lineage below. Without the resolve to give one's life in pursuit of the Way, how could anyone deserve that title?
To inherit the charge of peering into heaven has always required unshakable resolve. Yet this time, the two who entered the Duel of Blood burned with equal determination, one set on living, the other on dying.
Neither looked back as they walked toward the end.

zh:
“大哥，你看那小子使的枪法，怎么说？……哈哈哈哈，中原能人不少啊！”
屋檐上，伊刀醉醺醺地，对着手边的灰榇说道。自兄长离世，他一直将其骨灰带在身边。

说罢，他一跃而下，站到正在习武的某位江湖人身前。
“喂！老子看你练枪看腻了，来打一场。赢了我，就能活命。”
……
他为了磨炼武技，只身来到中原观摩各路武者侠士的比试，暗中拆解，一边默记一边思考破解之道。凡有一派武艺被他学成，伊刀便会找上门去，逞勇斗狠，不惜死伤。
就这样不知过了多少年，伊刀皮肉上各种刀疤剑痕不胜数，也终于武功大成。此刻，他只缺一把趁手的兵刃——
能陪着他出生入死、杀人越货的兵刃，百战不折，如臂驱使。 

终于，伊刀以天池玄铁为材，又将兄长骨灰洒入熔炉，铸得了那把他等候已久的兵刃——死人刀。 
“后面的血路，咱哥俩一起闯了。”

死人刀刃上的第一抹血，是伊刀自己的。他以此血，祭双亲，祭大哥，祭这杀伐不断的世间道。
而第二抹血，伊刀决心让它流自白云天，只为替大哥报仇。
en:
"Brother, what do you make of that kid's spear technique?... Hahaha, the Heartland has no lack of talent!"
Drunk on a rooftop, Yi Dao slurred at the gray urn beside him. He had carried his brother's ashes with him since the man's death.

With that, he leaped down and stood before a jianghu warrior practicing martial arts.
"Hey! I'm sick of watching you drill with that spear. Let's fight. Beat me, and you live."
...
To hone his skills, he had come to the Central Plain alone, observing duels between warriors and secretly dissecting their techniques, memorizing and puzzling out ways to counter them. Once he mastered a sect's martial arts, Yi Dao would seek out its practitioners, picking fights regardless of the risk of injury or death. 
Years passed, his skin crisscrossed with countless scars from blades and swords. At last, his martial arts reached perfection. Now, he lacked only one thing: a weapon that could match him in battle. A blade that would follow him through life and death, capable of murder and pillage, unbreakable after a hundred battles, as obedient as his arm.

Finally, using Tianchi meteoric iron, he sprinkled his brother's ashes into the furnace and forged the weapon he had long awaited: the Killerblade.
"We'll carve through the bloodshed together, brother."

The first drop of blood on the Killerblade was Yi Dao's own. With it, he honored his parents, his brother, and this world of endless slaughter.
The second drop, he vowed, would come from Bai Yuntian—to avenge his brother.

zh:
伊刀本以为自己会死在钟王筹的手上。
二人也曾做过一段时间的兄弟。钟王筹帮他寻得玄铁打造死人刀，是以他立下誓言不可用死人刀对钟王筹出手，即便是钟王筹给他下了剧毒，欲置他于死地。
倒下前，伊刀看到有个身穿白衣之人，拦在他的身前。
又有多管闲事之人，他想。

待伊刀再次醒来，身边已不见钟王筹的身影，只剩下那个白衣侠客。
此人自称是天泉弟子，名叫褚清泉。
伊刀平日里最是讨厌和这些名门正派的弟子扯上关系，没想到这次竟是被这人给救了。
“你和钟王筹有仇？”
“有也没有。”
“有就是有，没有就是没有，什么叫‘有也没有’？和你们这些人讲话真是累得慌！”
“……我来是想肃清十三凶徒。”
“哼，那老子也是十三凶徒。你杀了钟王筹算老子欠你的，你眼下可动手了。”
“我不杀你。”
“为什么？”
“你和那十二人不一样。”
这些正派之人说话弯弯绕绕，心思也是弯弯绕绕，一会儿要杀一会儿又不杀的，忒烦人。伊刀懒得去想这些复杂的问题，也没问自己和那十二人究竟有什么不一样。总之褚清泉救了他，他理应报答。
二人自此一道踏入了江湖，同行数年，直至褚清泉身死。

后人有云：
死人刀乃十二凶徒之第十三人，此人脾气暴躁、肆意妄为。褚清泉乃名门正派弟子，有赤子之心，匡扶正义。
此二人行事天差地别，本无交集。然死人刀重诺，褚清泉重义，二人实为至交。
褚清泉亡故后，伊刀受其嘱托只身前往神仙渡，其一生，从未食言。
en:
Yi Dao always thought he'd die at the hands of Zhong Wangchou.
The two of them had once even been sworn brothers. Zhong Wangchou had helped him find the rare metal needed to forge the Killerblade, so Yi Dao had sworn never to use that blade against him, even when Zhong Wangchou later poisoned him, intent on killing him.
Just before he collapsed, Yi Dao caught a glimpse of someone in white stepping in front of him.
Another nosy do-gooder, he thought.
When Yi Dao woke again, Zhong Wangchou was gone. Only the white-clad swordsman remained.

This man introduced himself as Chu Qingquan, a Well of Heaven disciple.Yi Dao had always hated getting mixed up with righteous sect types, yet it was one of them who'd saved him this time.
"Do you have a grudge against Zhong Wangchou?"
"Maybe I do, maybe I don't."
"It's either yes or no. What's with this'maybe' business? Talking to people like you is exhausting!"
"...I'm here to eliminate the Thirteen Fiends."
"Hmph. Well, I'm one of them. Since you killed Zhong Wangchou, let's say I owe you one. If you want to kill me, now's your chance."
"I won't kill you."
"Why not?"
"You're different from the other twelve."
People from these righteous sects always talked in circles and changed their minds every other minute. Yi Dao couldn't be bothered to figure it all out, nor did he care to ask how he was different from the others. All he knew was that Chu Qingquan had saved him, and he owed him.
From then on, the two of them wandered the martial world together for years, until the day Chu Qingquan died.

Later, people would say:
The Killerblade was the thirteenth among the notorious Thirteen Fiends, hot-tempered, reckless, and uncontrollable. Chu Qingquan was a disciple of an esteemed sect, pure-hearted and devoted to justice.
By rights, they should never have crossed paths. But Killerblade valued loyalty, and Chu Qingquan valued righteousness, and so the two became the closest of friends.
After Chu Qingquan's death, Yi Dao honored his final request and set off alone for Heaven's Pier, never breaking his word throughout his life.

它又是一只很安静的小猫，以至于同样住在水边的人一直都没有发现它。直到人家中购置了新船，船蒿拨开田田的莲叶，人才第一次听到一声轻轻的：“喵——”
人放下船篙再想去找猫，已经找不到了。
人回去就跟隔壁邻居、对面邻居都讲了这个故事。
故事里有大片大片的莲叶，有刚刚探出来的小荷尖尖，有那一天顺着水吹过来的风，有水波里倒映出来的天和云，还有那一声轻轻的喵。
人给这声喵起了个名字，叫作水水。
不知道水水会不会知道自己叫这个名字。不过杭州的水流得这样悠长，会流进人的心里，也会流进小猫的心里。
en:
The folk of Hangzhou all dwell by the water, and so too do the cats. Water is just such a cat, one who makes its home along the waterside.
It was also a remarkably quiet cat, so quiet that the people living nearby the water had never once noticed it, not until the family bought a new boat, and the punting pole parted the dense lily pads, that they first heard a soft little "Meow..."
The man set down his pole and went looking for the cat, but it was nowhere to be found.
When he returned home, he told the story to the neighbors.
In that story there were vast stretches of lotus leaves, tender new shoots just beginning to peek above the water, the breeze that drifted in over the water that day, the sky and clouds reflected in the rippling waves, and that one soft little meow.
The man gave that little meow a name: Water.
Whether Water knows it bears this name, no one can say. But the waters of Hangzhou flow on so long and unhurried that they seep into the hearts of people, and just as surely, into the hearts of little cats.

zh:
花解语的擅饮是天生的。她从来都喝不醉，除非她自己想醉。
凭这个本事，她饮过了不知多少佳酿：开封的醉仙饮、江南的丰和春、蜀地的竹叶青…… 都甜丝丝的，令人欢喜。
她只在刚入醉花阴的那一年醉过一回。虽因醉中姿容得了一个“海棠花”的诨名，却也第一次让她明白，原来同门的前辈没有骗她，酒也可以是涩的。——自此之后，她再没醉过。
直到兜兜转转，不知多少年后，她遇到了一个年轻的游侠。
那人捧着一瓮海棠酒，满头是汗地看着她，眼睛里装着的都是真挚与热切。花解语看着那人的眼睛，忽然又懂了前辈们的一句话，原来乱世中的天真与良善，真的很动人。
好似这么些年的酒力都在这一瞬涌了上来。花解语忽然觉得自己很困，连自己随身携带多年的玉环掉入酒盏，都没有发觉。
“就再醉一会吧。比春天还要短的那么一小会。”
花解语想着，卧在那人身边，轻轻合上了眼。
en:
Hua Jieyu was born with a gift for drinking—she never got drunk unless she wanted to.
Thanks to this talent, she had tasted countless fine wines: Drunken Immortal Wine from Kaifeng, Spring's Bounty from Jiangnan, Bamboo Leaf from Shu... all sweet and delightful.
She'd only ever been drunk once, the year she first joined the Velvet Shade. That one time earned her the nickname "Crabapple Flower" for her tipsy beauty—but also taught her that the seniors hadn't lied: wine could be bitter too. She never got drunk again.
Until, after many years, she met a young wanderer.
He stood before her, sweating, clutching a jar of Crabapple Wine, eyes full of earnest warmth. As she looked into those eyes, she suddenly understood another lesson from her elders: in a chaotic world, innocence and kindness truly move the heart.
It felt as if all those years of resistance to wine came crashing down at once. She grew drowsy, so much so she didn't notice the jade ring she always carried fall into the cup.
"Just a little longer... drunk for a moment, as short as spring."
With that thought, Hua Jieyu lay beside him, and gently closed her eyes.

zh:
古之花毽，天罡地煞，招数繁多。余取其精要，得三十六路。
一招一法，俱有口诀。记诵在心，方得其门。宜勤加练习，足堪行走江湖。

足内旋，身徐转，毽似柳叶不离畔。
膝磕毽，步稳沉，敌未动时我先临。

脚尖蹦，眼先行，人随毽翻心气平。

招式可学，心法难传。毽之飞落，犹人起伏。
待毽以诚，不以假招欺己，不以毽偏生怒。
毽不欺足，人不欺心。行诸待人，其道一也。
en:
The ancient art of shuttlecock encompassed the full host of heavenly and earthly techniques, countless in number. I have distilled their essence into thirty-six forms.
Each move and method comes with its own mnemonic verse. Commit them to memory, and you shall find the way in. Practice diligently, and you'll be well-equipped to walk the Jianghu.
...
Coiling, striking, twisting, leaping. These four techniques form the foundation.
...
The foot turns inward, the body slowly spins, the shuttlecock clings like a willow leaf never straying far.
The knee strikes the shuttlecock, the stance steady and grounded. Before the foe even moves, I have already arrived.
The reverse kick channels power from the waist, and turning back, a startled swan rises to the sky.
The toes leap, the eyes lead first, the body follows the shuttlecock as the heart settles calm.
...
The moves can be learned, but the inner way is hard to pass on. The rise and fall of the shuttlecock mirrors the rise and fall of a person's life.
Treat the shuttlecock with sincerity. Do not deceive yourself with false technique, nor grow angry when the shuttlecock strays.
The shuttlecock does not betray the foot; a person should not betray their own heart. To carry this into how one treats others—that is the same path.

en:
As a boy, Jiang Yan once walked the streets with Wang Qing when they spotted a thief stealing purses from passing travelers. Wang sprang into action and caught the criminal. Passersby praised him and called him a true hero. Jiang, eyes wide with admiration, declared that one day he too would be known across the land, a great hero all would call "Great Hero Jiang."  Wang Qing asked what would he do next after he fulfilled his dream, and Jiang Yan said to protect him. Wang paused for a long moment. 

"There was once someone who said the same to me. You two are quite alike." 
"Really?! Did he succeed? Did he become a great hero?" 
"He did."

zh:
话说那怪味角黍被璎璎女侠救下后，便在开封城里出了名。人们听说了璎璎女侠的事迹，纷纷想要尝一口这怪味角黍，就连这驿站的信使也不例外。
这天，他刚从睡梦中醒来，便收到了……璎璎女侠寄给大侠的信件！和信件一起的，竟还有一笼角黍！
他颤抖着双手捧起这一笼角黍，内心已是抑制不住的激动：这该不会就是，自己日思夜想、梦寐以求的怪味角黍吧！可是……这是寄给别人的，自己绝不能独占！
就在此时，他听见一个如鞭子般的声音，喊了自己的名字！原来是驿长要找他，他只好放下角黍，慌忙赶去。
等再回来时，他绝望地发现——璎璎女侠的信件已被车夫带走，而那一笼角黍竟被落下了！
于是他找到另外一名车夫，拜托他快马加鞭地将角黍带给大侠。
车夫听闻，日夜兼程。而这笼怪味角黍，终于来到了大侠的手中！
en:
So it came to pass that the strange-flavored Zongzi, having been rescued by the swordswoman Yingying, grew famous throughout the city of Kaifeng. Word of Yingying's deeds spread far and wide, and everyone longed to taste but a bite of these curious Zongzi. Even the courier at the relay station was no exception.
That day, no sooner had he woken from sleep than he received... a letter from Yingying, addressed to the great hero! And alongside the letter, there was even a basket of Zongzi!
With trembling hands he cradled the basket, unable to suppress his excitement. Could this truly be the strange-flavored Zongzi he had longed for day and night, dreamed of even in his sleep! But... this was meant for another; he could not claim it for himself alone!
Just then, he heard a voice sharp as a whip crack, calling out his name! It was the station master seeking him. He had no choice but to set down the Zongzi and hurry off in a fluster.
When he returned, he discovered to his despair that the coachman had already taken away Yingying's letter, but the basket of Zongzi had been left behind!
So he sought out another coachman and begged him to make haste, riding swiftly to deliver the Zongzi to the great hero.
Hearing this, the driver rode day and night without rest. And so, at last, this basket of strange-flavored Zongzi arrived in the great hero's hands!

前几日听乡亲说，夜半山林里有幽幽的鬼火飘来飘去，还能发出人的动静，大家都认为是撞鬼了，我偏不信！必是有人在暗中捣鬼才对。
于是我在林子里埋伏，一蹲便是两整天。夜里山风刺骨，吹得头疼，吃完了干粮，只能捡些野果充饥，还有不少马猴把我当成了来抢地盘的，一直朝我扔石子。不过一想到能破获大案，咬咬牙也都忍下来了，可谁承想呢！
我好不容易逮住那鬼火，仔细一瞅，竟然是两个墨门弟子！说是在搞什么照明实验……我的大案就这么没了。
回去的时候，我碰见了徐婶子，她看我一身草屑的狼狈样，笑着塞给我几个煮鸡蛋。唉，虽然大案是没破成，不过想想，没有人因此受伤，鬼怪流言也被解释清了……是好事，是好事吧。
en:
A few days ago, some villagers told me about strange ghostly lights drifting through the woods in the middle of the night, with noises that sounded almost human. Everyone else was convinced the place was haunted. I wasn't buying it. Someone had to be pulling tricks in the dark.
So I staked out the forest and stayed there for two full days. At night, the mountain wind was bitterly cold and gave me a pounding headache. Once I ran out of dry rations, I had to fill my stomach with wild fruit. On top of that, quite a few macaques decided I was there to steal their turf and kept lobbing stones at me. Still, the thought of cracking a big case kept me going, so I gritted my teeth and endured it all. But guess what?
When I finally caught up to the "ghostly light" and got a good look at it, it turned out to be two Mohist disciples doing some sort of lighting experiment... And just like that, my big case was gone.
On the way back, I ran into Auntie Xu. She took one look at me, covered in bits of grass and looking thoroughly miserable, and laughed as she stuffed a few boiled eggs into my hands. Well... I may not have cracked the big case after all, but no one was hurt, and the ghost rumors were put to rest. So I suppose that's a good thing. Yes... a good thing.

zh:
胡二饼很喜欢睡觉。因为他每次睡觉，都能梦见他的老狗。
梦里，老狗蹒跚着向他跑来，亲昵地钻进他的怀里，粗壮的尾巴打着他的腿。真奇怪，人在梦里是不会痛的，可胡二饼却总觉得小腿被老狗的尾巴打得生疼。胡二饼不舍得说老狗，只是一味地蹂躏着老狗的头。
他在梦里和老狗有了个家，就在坎尔孜。他还和老狗背着干粮去沙漠里冒险。一人一狗，就像开始的那样。
美梦总会醒来。胡二饼看着河西不落的暖阳，心里总是空落落的。
不过胡二饼手也没停下来。开馕坑，打饼，熬糖，又是辛苦劳累的一天。
胡二饼嚼着刚出炉的烤馕，看着孩子们围着自己吃玛仁糖，眼里乐呵呵。
他揉了揉酸痛的肩膀，心满意足。
今天一定能睡得更沉，更香。
老狗一定还在梦里等着额咧，胡二饼开心地想。
en:
Hu Erbing loved to sleep. Because every time he slept, he dreamed of his old dog. 
In the dream, the old dog would hobble towards him, nuzzle affectionately into his arms, its sturdy tail thumping against his leg. So strange—people shouldn't feel pain in dreams, yet Hu Erbing always felt his calf stinging from those tail thumps. He couldn't bear to scold the dog, only endlessly ruffled its head. 
In the dream, he and the old dog had a home, right there in Karez. They even packed dry rations and went adventuring in the desert together. One man, one dog, just like at the very beginning. 
Good dreams always end. Hu Erbing would look at the never-setting warm sun of Hexi, his heart always feeling hollow. 
But Hu Erbing's hands never stopped. Lighting the naan oven, kneading dough, boiling syrup—another day of hard, weary work. 
Chewing on freshly baked naan, watching children crowd around eating walnut brittle, his eyes crinkled with joy. 
He rubbed his sore shoulders, content. 
Tonight, he would surely sleep deeper, more soundly. 
The old dog must still be waiting for him in the dream, Hu Erbing thought happily.

After the death of Chai Rong, Zhao Kuangyin donned the yellow robe at Chenqiao, claiming the mandate of the realm. Li Jun refused to acknowledge the new sovereign and raised his banners, marching south. Murong Yanzhao and Shi Shouxin set out from two fronts to flank Li Yun. 
Once sworn friends, now enemies with blades in hands on the battlefield. 
At the gates of Zezhou, Li Jun was defeated. He cast himself into the flames. Murong Yanzhao stood still as the fire roared, staring across the inferno at the outline of his old friend. Blood and tears ran down his sword, hissing into the scorched earth, and vanished in an instant. 
Just like everything they once shared.

zh: 常盛集者，青州之盛市也。其址踞葱王坪前，与村落相去咫尺。每逢朔望，义集开市三日，商旅不绝；余日则摊空人稀，俨然两般天地。市集之日，行人如织，摩肩接踵。若遇奇货，则列队如龙，此乃青州一大奇观也。
en: The Everbloom Bazaar is the most bustling bazaar in Qingzhou. Situated right in front of the Crownleek Terrace, it lies only a stone's throw away from the local villages. On the days of the new and full moon, this public market opens for three consecutive days, drawing an endless stream of merchants and travelers. On ordinary days, however, the stalls sit empty and the crowds vanish, making it look like two completely different worlds. On market days, pedestrians weave through the streets, rubbing shoulders and following closely on each other's heels. Whenever rare and exotic goods appear, people line up like a long dragon. This vibrant scene is truly one of the great spectacles of Qingzhou.

zh:
阿蒲记着它没尝过冰葡萄。可当它需要个名字时，那股清冽的甜香突然窜进鼻腔——就决定是蒲了！
阿蒲常趴在安一飞膝头，听酡婆婆跟安一飞感慨：谁走了，谁死了，谁家孩子蹿高了。半梦半醒间，小猫觉着好像从前决定过要替谁多看几眼牵挂的人。现在，他们都与挂念的人好好道别了吗？
阿蒲记不得，阿蒲想不通，阿蒲眯着眼瞧酡婆婆的笑纹，尾巴尖轻轻一拍，又沉进温暖的梦里。
en:
Grape had never tasted the icy grapes, but when it came time to choose a name, that fresh, sweet scent suddenly filled its nose—and so the name "Grape" was born. 
Half-dreaming in Granny's voice, the little cat felt as if it had once vowed to watch a little longer over those who mattered. Had everyone now found peace and said their goodbyes? 
Grape couldn't remember, couldn't quite understand—so it squinted at the gentle smile etched on Granny's face, flicked its tail softly, and sank back into the warmth of its dreams.

zh:
郑鄂一直记着与沈义伦的初见。瘦弱的孩子站在学堂的角落里，窃窃地告诉先生自己的志向。他说，“只要能吃饱饭，做什么……都好。”
这种看起来毫无追求的理想，自然而然地遭到了同窗的讥笑。郑鄂没有笑，他想到了多年来开封的朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨；想到了不久前发生的契丹入寇，全城饥荒。他思索着，忽然便找到了自己的志向。
——“那便由我们让大伙儿都吃饱饭，让‘天下常平，黎民无饥’！”

郑鄂是这么许诺的，也是这么做的。他真诚地想让人人都活下去，完全料想不到自己的善意竟会换来一场毫无人性的屠戮，流寇们冲入宅院，见人就杀、见粮就抢，火光与哭声很快便连成一片，瞬间就吞没了少年天真而脆弱的理想。
“怎么会这样…… 我明明是想救人，可结果怎么会是这样……？”他跪在郑阮和众多亲友的尸体面前，失魂落魄。
因为善意而想要救一个好人，结果成全了一众恶徒，连累了无数无辜的人。
若放任好人不管，好人与恶徒都会死，其他人会活下去。可是对他人生死坐视不理者，又遑论无辜。
所以，是不是他从一开始就错了？郑鄂心想，会不会乱世之中根本就不该存在善良？

“你没有错。行善永远是对的。”
很久之后郑鄂才平复心绪，终于听清了侠客的回答。那时候那场暴乱已过去了数月，眠茔冢的荒地上，无数的新坟立起来。
“如果善良有错，那你我根本就不会相遇。”
侠客望着跪在坟前的郑鄂，说得坚定。郑鄂缓缓转过身来，将视线从墓碑挪到侠客身上。他细细打量着侠客，似乎在寻找着更多能让他信服的证据，直到他的目光最后落在侠客握紧的配剑上。
“你能够践行你的善良，因为你有力量。但我不能，因为我的手上没有刀？”
侠客被少年问得一愣，不知该如何作答。因为她在拔剑杀敌、行侠仗义的瞬间其实什么都没有想。她隐隐觉得不对，却没能继续思索下去，眼前的少年已砰砰地朝她磕了三个响头，他求她收自己为徒，因为他不想让惨剧再度发生，不想要丢掉自己的初心。
可乱世中的善良到底太过奢侈。于是当十年之后，连侠客也被浊世的洪流吞没了，郑鄂又不可遏制地再次陷入迷惘。——如果说行善的前提是拥有力量，那侠客、亲人，他们为什么会死？到底要站在什么样的高位上，才能够始终善良？
“不，不是因为力量，而是因为恶徒。是他们在制造悲剧、在催折善良。只要他们还活着，好人就只剩死路一条。”
已经长大的郑鄂思索着。这一次他缓缓将视线投向承恩镇、河清军……，投到这些恶人身上。——他握紧了手中的刀。
en:
Zheng E has never forgotten his first meeting with Shen Yilun. The scrawny boy stood in the corner of the schoolroom, whispering his ambition to the teacher: "As long as I have enough to eat, I'll do anything..."
Such a seemingly aimless dream was met with sneers from classmates. Zheng E did not laugh. He thought of Kaifeng's mansions wasting food while corpses froze in the streets, of the recent Khitan invasion that had starved the city. Suddenly, he found his own purpose.
"Then let us ensure everyone has enough to eat. Let there be'Ever-Normal for All! No hunger for the people'!"

Zheng E kept his word, and his deeds matched it. He truly wished for everyone to survive, never imagining that his kindness would be repaid with a massacre of utter savagery. The bandits stormed into the estate, slaughtering all in their path and looting every grain in sight. Flames and wails soon merged into a single, consuming tide, swallowing the boy's naive and fragile idealism in an instant.
"How could this be? ... I only wanted to save them... so why... why did it end like this...?" He knelt before the bodies of Zheng Ruan and so many loved ones, his spirit shattered.
Trying to save one good man had empowered a horde of villains, dooming the innocent.
If he let good people suffer, both the virtuous and the wicked would die, but others might survive. But how could those who stood by be called innocent?
Was I wrong from the start? he wondered. Is there no place for kindness in a chaotic world?

"You were not wrong. Doing good is always right."
It took Zheng E months to hear the swordsman's words over the roar of his grief.
By then, the riot had left Withershade Mound crowded with new graves.
"If kindness were a sin, we would never have met."
The swordsman gazed at Zheng E kneeling before the graves, his voice resolute. Zheng E turned slowly, his gaze lifting from the tombstone to rest upon the swordsman. He studied the man intently, as if searching for further proof to trust him, until at last, his eyes settled on the sword clenched tightly at the warrior's side.
"You can act on your kindness because you have power. But I can't, because I don't have a sword?"
The swordsman hesitated. She had never questioned why she drew her blade to fight, she just did. Before she could think, the boy knocked his head three times on the ground, begging to be her disciple. He refused to let such tragedy happen again, he would not lose his original heart.
But kindness in troubled times is a luxury. A decade later, when even the swordsman fell to the tide of corruption, Zheng E spiraled into doubt again. If power is the prerequisite for goodness, why did the swordsman and my family die? What position of power allows one to stay kind forever?
"No, it's not about power. It's about the evildoers. They create tragedies, they destroy kindness. As long as they live, good people have no choice but to die."
The grown Zheng E stared at Gracetown, Heqing Army... at the villains. He tightened his grip on his sword.

【闵公第四】

元年，春，王正月。

○齐人救邢。

庄公葬而后举谥，谥所以成德也。于卒事乎加之矣。
○秋，八月，公及齐侯盟于洛姑。季子来归。
盟纳季子也。其曰季子，贵之也。其曰来归，喜之也。
○冬，齐仲孙来。
其曰齐仲孙，外之也。其不目而曰仲孙，疏之也。其言齐，以累桓也。

……
en:
【Duke Min, Volume Four】

First Year, Spring, the King's first month.
Not mentioning succession upon the death of a ruler is correct. Though related, he was not the father; though honored, he was not the ruler. Succeeding as if he were both ruler and father, he received the state accordingly.
○ Qi rescued Xing.
This praises the rescue of Xing.
○ Summer, Sixth Month, Xinyou, we buried our ruler, Duke Zhuang.
Only after Duke Zhuang's burial was his posthumous name conferred; the posthumous name completes one's virtue. It is added upon the completion of the funeral rites.
○ Autumn, Eighth Month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Luo Gu. Ji Zi returned.
The alliance was to install Ji Zi. Calling him Ji Zi honors him. Saying he "returned" expresses joy at his arrival.
○ Winter, Qi's Zhongsun came.
Calling him Qi's Zhongsun sets him apart. Not naming him directly but calling him Zhongsun distances him. Mentioning Qi implicates Duke Huan.

②回收：被套产业的设施总量多余图纸中同类设施时，套用图纸后会回收超出的设施到仓库

③保留：套用图纸时，被套产业没有回收的设施，会自动挪动到图纸的设施位置
en:
Applying a Diagram with Industry Facilities may result in the addition, retention, or recycling of facilities.

①Addition: Facilities in the Diagram not present in the Industry or Warehouse will be placed as holograms and can be filled manually.

②Recycle: If the Industry has more facilities of a certain type than the Diagram, excess facilities will be returned to the Warehouse.

③Retention: Facilities not recycled during application will be automatically moved to the positions specified in the Diagram.

zh:
批《墨家百种行水枢机演变图录》：

执于全而拙于思，偏于幽微而无大局。尽录其类机枢百年，无需多析，义理流变，已自现尔。
然水，变化之物，非拘于一时一处。不为则已，为，则算四时，划方圆，联万里，安八荒。
昔者禹之功，疏天下水而留法万代。至于今人，尽得先贤之智，又有机关术为助，不立旷古之业，则万卷经书、岂不枉读？可效之矣！
en:
A Critique of Illustrated Records on the Evolution of Mohist Hydraulic Mechanisms:

This work pursues completeness at the expense of thought, dwelling on the minute while lacking any broader vision. It records in full the various mechanisms developed over the course of a hundred years; there is no need for excessive analysis, for the shifts in principle and method already reveal themselves.
Yet water is a thing of change, not something confined to one moment or one place. If one does not act, so be it. But if one does, one must reckon with the four seasons, mark out square and round, link lands across ten thousand miles, and bring order to the eight reaches of the realm.
In ages past, Yu the Great tamed the floods of the world and left methods to later generations. We today have inherited the wisdom of the ancients, and we also have the aid of mechanical arts. If we fail to found an undertaking worthy of all ages, then have we not read our myriad books in vain? It is something we should strive to emulate.
Gong Jiang Mao You You

张家长子已在佛前跪了五日。他在后悔。

僧人再次踏入佛堂，将一块玄铁放在他面前。
令弟未死，尚有弥补之机。知多者智多，你所做无错，只是尚不足够矣。

他抚上玄铁，家丁自外飞奔而来，带来小弟醒来的消息。他狂喜起身，踉跄着往佛堂外冲去。

en:
The eldest Zhang son had knelt before the Buddha for five days. He was filled with regret. 
Regret that he taught his younger brother swordsmanship but not how to protect himself while using it. 
So when his brother took a blade to champion justice, a moment's lapse left him gravely wounded—all the elder brother's fault. 

The monk entered the hall again, placing a piece of dark iron before him. 
Your brother lives, and there is still time. More knowledge brings more wisdom. You did nothing wrong—you simply did not do enough.

“娘？娘早被他打跑了。我不怪我娘，谁都想活命。留在那个家里，只有死路一条。”
“阿姐本也可以逃的，但那会儿我太小了，她没忍心。“
“所以，是阿姐带大了你？”
“是，若没有阿姐，我兴许早就成了村口那老树下的一滩烂泥。”
“所以我一定要找到阿姐。即便是一具枯骨，也得亲眼见了，亲手葬了，才能安心。”
话至此，姜隗停了一瞬手上的动作。不知何时下起了雨，乱葬岗里一片泥泞，他一身白衣被溅上了不少污泥，斑斑点点，似是血迹。
而眼前不远处，泥土被冲刷后，露出了木簪的一角。是一朵残缺的梅花。他刻这个簪子时才十岁，手笨，刻了几天几夜，还是刻坏了。本想扔了重新开始，但阿姐拦住了他。
那时阿姐笑着同他说，那是世上最美的梅花。
而现在，那世上最美的梅花，和他最爱美的阿姐，一同被埋葬在这污泥中。
木花腐朽，人化枯骨。
en:
"When I was five, my father racked up gambling debts and was beaten badly by the collectors."

"He wanted to take it out on me. It was my sister who threw herself in front of me... The scar on her forehead—she got it that night."

"What about your mother?"

"Mother? She ran away long ago, could not bear father's violence. I don't blame her. Anyone would want to survive. Staying in that house... meant certain death for her."

"My sister could have run too, but I was too young. She couldn't leave me behind."

"So it was your sister who raised you?"

"Yes. Without her, I'd probably be nothing but a rotting corpse beneath the old tree at the village gate."

"That's why I have to find her. Even if all that's left is a pile of bones, I need to see her with my own eyes. And lay her to rest with my own hands."

Jiang Wei paused, his hands freezing for a moment. At some point, rain had begun to fall, turning the Mass Grave into a mire. His white robes were stained with mud, blotched like splattered blood. Not far ahead, the washed-out earth revealed the tip of a wooden hairpin, it's a broken plum flower. He had carved that hairpin when he was ten, clumsy and earnest, working days and nights, only to botch it. He had wanted to throw it away and start a new one, but his sister stopped him.

Smiling, she told him it was the most beautiful plum flower in the world. 

Now they lay buried together in the mud. That flower, and the sister he loved the most.

Wood rots. Flesh turns to bone.

zh:
世上有什么物件，永远不会变，不会碎，想起的时候总能见到？ 
聪明的人，会说是江海。因为水珠从不碎裂，只是融进江海之中。 
智慧的人，可能会想到月光。因为江水年年来去，只有月光依然照亮人间。 
  
“我知道，是——谷米花！” 
小米仔响亮地答。 
小孩的世界里没有那些汹涌的江海和月光，只有永恒的零嘴儿！谷米花不会变少，想吃的时候，永远都在！如果随身的小口袋瘪了，就对姆妈说。很快，袋子里又会装满香喷喷的谷米花了。 
  
“笨！谷米花最容易坏了！那些都是你姆妈悄悄塞到口袋里的！” 
  
真的吗？小米仔瘪瘪嘴，要放声大哭啦。大人们才是笨蛋，他们根本就不懂！姆妈的抱抱，姆妈的歌声，甜丝丝的谷米花……世上不变不碎的东西，实在太多啦！根本犯不着去月亮上和江海里找！ 
“我就是对的，我就是对的嘛……”小米仔打开珍爱的小口袋，又掏出一捧谷米花塞进嘴里。 
  
很久很久以后，小米仔到了长安。他的小口袋丢了，衣服也穿不下了。他开始长高，长壮，甚至有一天长出白花花的胡子来了。 
  
世上有什么物件，永远不会变，不会碎，想起的时候总能见到？ 
  
米嘉荣仰着小脑袋问他。是从宫中赏赐下来的金银吗，是刻在石碑上的名字吗，是他双眼中年复一年流泻出的江海，和每个夜晚都陪在他床边的月光吗？ 
  
他已经长大了，变得很聪明，很智慧了。他心中有一个很聪明，很智慧的答案。 
  
“是谷米花，”小米仔对孩子说。 
  
“是姆妈装进口袋里的谷米花呀。”
en:
What thing in this world never changes, never shatters, and can always be seen whenever you think of it? 
A clever person might say it is the rivers and seas. Because water droplets never shatter, they simply merge into the rivers and seas. 
A wise person might think of moonlight. Because rivers come and go year after year, yet only the moonlight still illuminates the mortal world. 
 
"I know, it's Puffed Grain!" 
Xiao Mizi proclaimed loudly. 
In a child's world, there are no turbulent rivers and seas or moonlight, only eternal snacks! Puffed Grain never runs out, whenever you want to eat it, it's always there! If the little pouch at your side goes flat, just tell Mom. Soon, the pouch will be filled again with fragrant Puffed Grain. 
 
"Fool! Puffed Grain spoils the easiest! Those are all secretly stuffed into your pouch by Mom!" 
 
Really? Xiao Mizi pouted, about to burst into tears. Adults are the fools, they just don't understand! Mom's hugs, Mom's songs, sweet Puffed Grain... There are so many things in the world that never change or break. No need to look for them in the moon or rivers! 
"I'm right, I'm right!... " Xiao Mizi opened his cherished little pocket and pulled out another handful of Puffed Grain to stuff into his mouth. 
 
Many, many years later, Xiao Mizi went to Chang'an. His little pouch was lost, and his clothes no longer fit. He grew taller and stronger, until one day, white beard hairs grew on his chin. 
 
What thing in this world never changes, never shatters, and can always be seen whenever you think of it? 
 
Mi Jiarong looked up at him with a small head. Was it the gold and silver rewarded by the palace? The name carved on the stone tablet? The rivers and seas flowing from his eyes year after year, or the moonlight that accompanied him by his bed every night? 
 
He had grown up now, becoming very clever, very wise. He had a very clever, very wise answer in his heart. 
 
"It's Puffed Grain," Xiao Mizi said to the child. 
 
"It's the Puffed Grain that Mom put into the pouch."

油馍
油馍是一种常见的面点，在各个地方有不同的做法。但在中原常常是将洒入切碎的花椒叶和葱的面团，打上油，来回揉，揉的差不多了再打一遍油，直到面团有层为止。人便是这样对自己的：遇到一个个难关时，总有谁的眼泪陪着一起掉下来润滑，于是这难关便过去了。油馍好吃就好吃在它既有外面略焦发硬的部分，又有内里一层层软喧的里子。而每一层里子，都咸咸的，好吃。
en:
10. Youmo

Youmo is a common wheat pastry, and every region has its own way of making it. In the Central Plains, the dough is mixed with chopped huajiao leaves and scallions, brushed with oil, then kneaded again and again. More oil, more kneading, until it builds up layers.

People aren't so different. When hardship comes one after another, someone always ends up crying with you, and those tears somehow help things go down easier. And somehow, you get through.

That's why youmo is so good: a lightly crisp, slightly firm outside, and soft, fluffy layers within. Each layer carries a gentle saltiness, and it's delicious.

en:
Mirkvale lies at the northern foot of Mohist City and is famed throughout the mountain for its skill in metalworking. Its water-diversion mechanisms are especially ingenious, channeling water to drive wheels and bellows and power the forges. Because of this, its blast furnaces burn day and night, and many of the Mohists' finest artisans gather here. In years past, the former Grandmasters Raven and Halcyon, along with the master artisan Zhang Wanshi, all studied here.
But an old tale, told half in jest, lured the Qiongqi Artificers into the valley in search of something. After that, the mechanisms fell still, the forge went silent, and the furnaces died. Now only a young boy named Xiaoba slips back into the valley to repair what he can. This journey may be urgent, but it is no less dangerous.

屋外的大黄狗立刻跑到了主人面前，没错，它的名字也叫黄芪。
它动了动狗鼻子，空气中的药味苦苦的。其实它还有个发现，那就是这里“人味”也苦苦的。
黄芪早就发现来这儿的人有些不一样，他们有的是被抬进来的；有的进门时拄着棍子，弯着腰，像是有三只脚；有的还没进门呢，就“哐当”一下倒在了门口，嘴角斜斜地流出一滩白沫。黄芪凑近闻过，的确是苦的。
它的主人宣莲常常一边抓药，一边望着他们叹气，然后叮嘱着些什么。
狗随主人，久而久之，黄芪也学会了。每当铺子里有人来看病，它就乖乖地陪在他们旁边，有时叼来肉骨头，有时蹭蹭他们的裤腿，还学着主人的样子对着他们“汪汪”有词。一位心通百兽的大侠翻译了一下，黄芪说的是——“人，你不要苦苦的，希望下次闻到你，是甜甜的。”
en:
"Two parts red jujube, one part Ginseng..." As soon as Xuan Lian, the owner of the Wansheng Town pharmacy, finishes speaking, the big yellow dog outside immediately runs to his owner. Yes, his name is also Ginseng.
He twitches his nose: the medicine in the air smells bitter. He has also noticed something else: the "human smell" here is bitter too.
Ginseng long ago found that the people who come here are different. Some are carried in. Some enter leaning on sticks, bent over as if they have three feet. Some collapse at the doorstep before even entering, a stream of white foam dribbling from the corner of their mouths. Ginseng sniffs them, definitely bitter. His owner, Xuan Lian, often sighs as he prepares their medicine, giving them instructions.
Like owner, like dog. Over time, Ginseng learns. Whenever someone comes to the pharmacy, he quietly stays by their side. Sometimes he brings them meaty bones. Sometimes he rubs against their pant legs. And just like his owner, he "woofs" at them meaningfully. A wandering knight who understands animals translates: what Ginseng says is, "Human, don't be bitter. I hope next time I smell you, you are sweet."

zh:
少东家台鉴：
离开家已然有些日子，虽是一路辛苦，但我这笔可没敢闲着。
可惜，这一路上的风儿甚为喧嚣，直搅得我脑中锣鼓齐鸣浆糊打架，几天了，竟也挤不出半篇像样的文字，我便索性卧乘小船随意漂流，无意中竟闯入一片桃源，打探才知，此地竟就是传说当中的墨门所在，“不见山”本山是也。
我见此地清幽，想着借山水雅韵给自己静静心，说不定能打通才思，就往山中闲行，没想到这下见识了什么叫人外有人，焦虑外有焦虑！
栈道旁、石崖下，竟坐了好些唉声叹气的墨门弟子。有位小哥手里的纸都快被捏皱了，恍惚念叨着“明日交稿明日愁，今日交稿命一条”，还有几人传阅着一张签卦，不知怎得竟让我拿到了，只见上面赫然写着“转发这个卦，明天考试不会挂”……
哈哈！看大家都这般焦头烂额，我就放心多啦！
我打算在这个好地方多待几日，少东家若是得空，不妨也来此走走，瞧瞧这深山里的别样景致。
正在赶稿的陆亢歌 敬上
en:
To the Young Master:
It's been a while since I left home. Though the journey is arduous, my pen hasn't dared to rest.
Unfortunately, the winds along the way have been so noisy they've turned my brain into a clashing mess of gongs and mush. It's been days, and I haven't managed to squeeze out even half a decent page. So, I just lay in a small boat and let it drift. Accidentally, I wandered into a utopia. I asked around and found out this place is the legendary site of the Mohist, the main peak of "Hidden Mountain" itself.
Seeing how serene it is, I thought I'd borrow the elegance of the landscape to calm my mind, maybe unclog my inspiration. So, I took a stroll into the mountains. Little did I know, I was about to witness that there's always someone more anxious out there!
By the plank roads and under the stone cliffs sat several sighing Mohist disciples. One young man was clutching his paper so tight it was almost entirely crumpled, muttering in a daze, "Tomorrow's deadline is tomorrow's sorrow; today's deadline takes my life away." A few others were passing around a fortune slip. Somehow, it ended up in my hands, and written boldly across it was: "Repost this sign, and your exams will go fine"...
Haha! Seeing everyone else pulling their hair out puts my mind completely at ease!
I plan to stay in this wonderful place for a few more days. If the Young Master has time, you should take a walk here too and see the unique scenery hidden deep in these mountains.
Writing furiously, Lu Kangge

[Music I]

[Qin]

Listening to the Monk Jun of Shu Play the Qin
Li Bai
The monk from Shu brings his lute of jade green; down from Mount Emei's peak he comes, serene.
He strums for me a single sweeping tone; as if I hear pines sigh in valleys lone.
My heart is cleansed by flowing stream's refrain; its lingering notes melt into frosty bell's strain.
Unaware, green hills have faded into night; autumn clouds have dimmed the sky's last light.

Listening to Lu Zishun Play the Qin Under the Moon
Li Bai
In the quiet night I sit beneath the moon so bright; the hermit plays his plain qin, a calming sight.
The tune of "Sad Wind" suddenly takes its flight; it echoes like the pines in winter's might.
"White Snow" dances beneath his flying hand; "Green Water" cleanses his heart, a tranquil land.
But Zhong Qi has long gone from this world's strand; no one alive can ever understand.

Listening to Monk Ying's Qin Song
Li He
Clouds leave the shore for Cassia Isle's domain; from Shu's strings come a pair of phoenixes' strain.
Lotus leaves fall, the autumn phoenix flies; the King of Yue by night to Tianmu hies.
Dark pendants worn by pure ministers ring; across the sea, fair brows lead white deer in spring.
Who sees the sword-bearer to Long Bridge stride? Who sees the hair-dipper write on bamboo's side?
The Dharmic monk stands forward at my gate; his brow's high ridge shows truth in solemn state.
The great qin's pegs are eight feet long and straight; old Fengyang wood, not from the tung-tree's fate.
In cool pavilion, strings startle this sick guest; my medicine bag I leave, my rush mat's rest.
Pray sing, but only for the lords and peers; what use is my low office through the years?

Playing the Qin on a Night Boat
Bai Juyi
The birds are perched, the fish lie still and deep; the moon shines on the river in the night so steep.
Outside myself, I have no worldly care; inside the boat, only the qin is there.
The seven strings are friends to me so true; my two ears are the listeners that knew.
When heart is still, the sound grows faint and low; in this I find no ancient or modern, just the flow.

[Zheng]

Listening to the Zheng
Li Duan
The golden-pegged zither sounds so grand; her fair hands play in the jade chamber's strand.
To win the master's lingering glance, with art; she strikes a wrong note now and then, with heart.

Zheng
Bai Juyi
Her cloud-like hair in greenish hues is dressed; her flower face in rosy red is blessed.
Her eyes can cut the autumn water's gleam; her fingers peel the spring onion's green stream.
The Chu's fair style is her noble gate; the Qin's clear tone is her skill innate.
Her silver nails are bright with polished shine; her jade pegs touch with tinkling chime divine.
The ape's sad cry complains the moon's late hour; the oriole's sweet voice speaks to the wind's power.
She draws her grief into her fingertips; she sends her sorrow through the strings and tips.
The Zhao zither's pure notes seem the same; the Hu fiddle's loud stirs a different flame.
A slow tune makes the wild geese seem to part; a quick one whirls the flying reed's art.
Her frost-like pendants tinkle and sway; her icy springs now choke, now flow away.
A thousand beats like pearls break in the air; one single cut ends the tune with a flare.
Her grace refined gives her spirit stead; her pride and skill her moods have wed.
When she stops, her feelings still remain; when she rests, her thoughts retain.
Beneath the lamp, this youth of spring night's time; before the cup, an old man in his prime.
I'll listen, for I ought to hear it all; my aging ears have not yet lost their call.

zh: 嫖姚棋，盛行于河西，是为了纪念汉代嫖姚将军-霍去病而设计的玩法。本身脱胎于盛行于长安的弹棋。弹棋，中国古代棋类游戏。沈括认为弹棋是起源于汉代，“汉元帝好蹴踘，以蹴踘为劳，求相类而不劳者，遂为弹棋之戏。”唐代是我国古代弹棋史上发展的一个高峰。这种靠技巧取胜的棋类游戏，不断成为文人吟咏的对象，杜甫、白居易、李贺、王涯、韦应物等均有诗作。王涯《宫词》中的“向晚移灯上银擎，丛丛绿鬃坐弹棋”，正是对在唐代广泛流行的弹棋的绝好描绘。
en: Piaoyao Battleboard, prevalent in Hexi, was designed to commemorate the Han Dynasty General Huo Qubing (titled "Piaoyao General"). It was derived from Danqi, which was popular in Chang'an. Shen Kuo believed Danqi originated in the Han Dynasty: "Emperor Yuan of Han enjoyed Cuju but found it tiring, so he sought something similar but less strenuous, thus creating Danqi." The Tang Dynasty marked the peak of Danqi's development, with this skill-based game frequently becoming a subject of poetry.

en:
It is said that a shared boat in a past life grants a shared pillow in this one. What great fortune, then, was mine to have met you, Lady Liu Si'an.

To be husband and wife for a day is to share mutual respect; for a hundred days, it is the bond of holding hands into old age. With you, I had wished to witness all of Chang'an's splendor, to sing long songs beneath the moon. To be a perfect couple, envied by others; to be true partners, celebrated by Heaven and Earth.

Alas, the passing years created a rift between us. Our lives were not our own to command, and the world is fraught with hardship and sorrow. You, Si'an, gentle as a willow, virtuous and kind, were yet unable to serve the elders above, nor manage the household below.

Today, I restore to you your freedom, hoping it brings you joy. I humbly pray that you, my lady, will find another good family. May you drink among blossoms and gaze upon the moon, with children and grandchildren gathered at your knees. May your family rejoice, and I, Shangguan, shall have no regrets.

This letter is set down as proof.

In Wannian County of Chang'an,

zh:
【告子章句下】

任人有问屋庐子曰：礼与食孰重？曰：礼重。色与礼孰重？曰：礼重。
曰：以礼食则饥而死；不以礼食则得食，必以礼乎？亲迎则不得妻，不亲迎则得妻，必亲迎乎？
屋庐子不能对。明日之邹，以告孟子。
孟子曰：于！答是也何有？不揣其本而齐其末，方寸之木，可使高于岑楼。金重于羽者，岂谓一钩金与一舆羽之谓哉？取食之重者与礼之轻者而比之，奚翅食重？取色之重者与礼之轻者而比之，奚翅色重？往应之曰：𬘝兄之臂而夺之食，则得食，不𬘝则不得食，则将𬘝之乎？逾东家墙而搂其处子，则得妻，不搂则不得妻，则将搂之乎？
曹交问曰：人皆可以为尧、舜，有诸？孟子曰：然。
交闻文王十尺，汤九尺，今交九尺四寸以长，食粟而已，如何则可？
曰：奚有于是？亦为之而已矣。有人于此，力不能胜一匹雏，则为无力人矣。今曰举百钧，则为有力人矣。则举乌获之任，是亦为乌获而已矣。夫人岂以不胜为患哉？弗为耳。徐行后长者谓之弟，疾行先长者谓之不弟。夫徐行者。岂人所不能哉！所不为也。尧、舜之道，孝弟而已矣。子服尧之服，诵尧之言，行尧之行，是尧而已矣。子服桀之服，诵桀之言，行桀之行，是桀而已矣。
曰：交得见于邹君。可以假馆。愿留而受业于门。
曰：夫道若大路然。岂难知哉？人病不求耳。子归而求之，有余师。
公孙丑问曰：高子曰：小弁，小人之诗也。孟子曰：何以言之？曰：怨。
曰：固哉，高叟之为诗也！有人于此，越人关弓而射之，则己谈笑而道之，无佗，疏之也。其兄关弓而射之，则己垂涕泣而道之，无佗，戚之也。小弁之怨，亲亲也。亲亲，仁也。固矣夫，高叟之为诗也！曰：凯风何以不怨？
曰：凯风，亲之过小者也；小弁，亲之过大者也。亲之过大而不怨，是愈疏也。亲之过小而怨，是不可矶也。愈疏，不孝也；不可矶，亦不孝也。孔子曰：舜其至孝矣。五十而慕。
宋牼将之楚，孟子遇于石丘，曰：先生将何之？
曰：吾闻秦、楚搆兵，我将见楚王说而罢之。楚王不悦，我将见秦王说而罢之。二王我将有所遇焉。
曰：轲也请无问其详，愿闻其指。说之将何如？
曰：我将言其不利也。

en:
【Gaozi, Part B】

A man from Ren asked Wulu Zi, "Which is more important, propriety or food?" Wulu Zi replied, "Propriety is more important." "Which is more important, desire or propriety?" "Propriety is more important."
The man said, "If one must follow propriety to eat, one will starve to death; if one does not follow propriety, one can get food. Must one then follow propriety? If one must perform the marriage ceremony to get a wife, one will not get a wife; if one does not perform it, one can get a wife. Must one then perform the marriage ceremony?"
Wulu Zi could not answer. The next day, he went to Zou and told Mencius about it.
Mencius said, "Ah! What difficulty is there in answering this? If you do not consider the foundation and only compare the ends, a piece of wood an inch square can be made to appear taller than a high tower. When we say metal is heavier than feathers, do we mean that a small hook of gold is heavier than a cartload of feathers? If you take the extreme case of food and compare it with the least important aspect of propriety, how can food not seem more important? If you take the extreme case of desire and compare it with the least important aspect of propriety, how can desire not seem more important? Go and reply to him thus: 'If by twisting your elder brother's arm and snatching his food you can get something to eat, but if you do not twist it you get nothing, will you then twist it? If by climbing over your eastern neighbor's wall and embracing his maiden daughter you can get a wife, but if you do not embrace her you get no wife, will you then embrace her?'"
Cao Jiao asked, "Is it true that anyone can become a Yao or a Shun?" Mencius said, "Yes."
Jiao said, "I have heard that King Wen was ten feet tall and Tang was nine feet tall. Now I am nine feet four inches tall, yet I can only eat millet. What should I do?"
Mencius said, "What has that to do with it? It is simply a matter of doing it. Suppose there is a man here who cannot lift a chick—he is then a man of no strength. But if he says he can lift a hundred jun, he is then a man of strength. So if he can lift the weight that Wu Huo lifted, he is just another Wu Huo. Why should a man worry about not being able? He simply does not do it. To walk slowly behind one's elders is called brotherly respect; to walk quickly ahead of one's elders is called disrespect. Now, walking slowly—is that something people cannot do? They simply do not do it. The way of Yao and Shun is nothing but filial piety and brotherly respect. If you wear the clothes of Yao, speak the words of Yao, and perform the actions of Yao, then you are Yao. If you wear the clothes of Jie, speak the words of Jie, and perform the actions of Jie, then you are Jie."
Jiao said, "I have obtained an audience with the lord of Zou. I can borrow a lodging. I wish to stay and receive instruction at your gate."
Mencius said, "The Way is like a great road. How could it be hard to know? The trouble with people is that they do not seek it. Go back and seek it, and you will find teachers in abundance."
Gongsun Chou asked, "Gaozi said, 'The "Xiao Pan" is the poem of a petty man.'" Mencius said, "Why did he say that?" "Because it expresses resentment."
Mencius said, "How rigid is Old Gao's interpretation of poetry! Suppose there is a man here. If a man from Yue draws his bow to shoot him, he will talk and laugh about it—for no other reason than that the man is a stranger. If his elder brother draws his bow to shoot him, he will weep and lament about it—for no other reason than that he is his kin. The resentment in 'Xiao Pan' is the affection for kin. Affection for kin is benevolence. How rigid indeed is Old Gao's interpretation of poetry!" Gongsun Chou asked, "Then why does 'Kai Feng' not express resentment?"
Mencius said, "'Kai Feng' deals with a minor fault of a parent; 'Xiao Pan' deals with a major fault of a parent. If a parent has a major fault and one does not resent it, that is to become more distant. If a parent has a minor fault and one resents it, that is to be overly agitated. To become more distant is unfilial; to be overly agitated is also unfilial. Confucius said, 'Shun was the most filial of all. At fifty, he still longed for his parents.'"
Song Keng was about to go to Chu. Mencius met him at Shiqiu and said, "Where are you going, sir?"
Song Keng said, "I have heard that Qin and Chu are at war. I am going to see the king of Chu and persuade him to stop. If the king of Chu is not pleased, I will go to see the king of Qin and persuade him to stop. I expect to meet with success with one of the two kings."
Mencius said, "I do not wish to ask for details, but I would like to hear the gist of your argument. How will you persuade them?"
Song Keng said, "I will tell them that it is not to their advantage."

en:
Not long after Zhang Wanshi returned to the mountain, Halcyon and Raven began visiting at different times. When they did show up together, things felt nothing like before.
Zhang Wanshi was never good with people, but he knew the two of them well enough to sense something was coming. At the heart of Lake of Guilt, he found a tri-colored stone and patiently ground it down into a ring. He thought that if his junior sister and junior brother came by again, he could give it to them.
He was not one for comforting words. He figured that if they saw the ring, they would understand, in their own way, what he meant as their senior brother. When they were young, they had shared a single dream. Even if the world turned harsh and changeable, they would still hold to it together.
But after that, the three of them never met again.

可惜蜀地遥远，传闻多奇异，我见过的绣球花总为白色，紫绣球传闻不可尽信。
en:
Brother Ge, I specifically consulted the agricultural texts of the Jadestream Valley region. There are no records supporting your claim that fertilizer affects chrysanthemum color.
However, there are records stating that in Shu, outside the mountains, there is a color-changing Hydrangea. It blooms green at first, then gradually turns pink. Using wood ash or fruit pulp... perhaps water, soil, and fertilizer really can affect the flower's appearance.
Pity that Shu is far away, and rumors are often strange. The hydrangeas I've seen are always white; rumors of purple hydrangeas cannot be fully trusted.

zh:
“许家三娘歌声婉转，一定能讨得天子与贵妃欢喜。”
教坊使的赞美她从来不敢相信。
“声有误者，帝必觉而正之。”梨园由天子筹办，对于乐曲方面，皇帝比任何人都懂，出不得丝毫差错。
第一次入宫献艺的梨园弟子，当然是不敢抬起头的。
她战战兢兢，甚至不知道该把手脚放在什么位置。
“十三岁，还是个小娃娃呢。”
贵妃的声音温润得恰到好处。许三娘悄悄抬眼，只瞥见浅笑的梨涡，像极了此时的满园春光。

皇帝要把自己新谱的曲子，让伶人唱与贵妃听。
据说是采曲人搜罗的乡间小调，唱男子思慕爱人，辗转反侧。
帝王爱人，高高在上赐予天下最难得的珍宝，却又要效仿百姓的姿态，捧出略显局促的真心。

许三娘唱得小心翼翼，她很清楚，自己唱得不差，但也不算好。
教坊之中都是千挑万选来的人才，不好，就是错。
等待审判的时刻，那个声音传来“小娃儿，过来。”
三娘几乎要踩到自己的裙摆，磕磕绊绊上前。
贵妃噗嗤一笑。纤纤玉指拿着朱红的果子塞进她手里，说自己很是欢喜。

之后天子和贵妃说了什么，她没听进去，仿佛帝王在问，自己能得到怎般奖赏。
声音低沉威严，又仿佛带着几分讨好。
教坊的伶人们纷纷谢安领赏，梨园春光，且留予男子和他的爱人共赏。

自乐师家出生，她被选入宫，编入教坊，一切似乎水到渠成。
踏出宫门的那一刻，三娘暗自想，或许自己是喜欢唱歌的。
en:
"Xu Sanniang has a voice like silk. Surely she'll charm both the Emperor and the Noble Consort." 
Sanniang never dared believe the overseer's praise. 
"One wrong note, and His Majesty will hear it at once." The Masked Troupe existed by imperial will; in matters of music, no one surpassed the Emperor's ear. There was simply no room for mistakes. 
For first‑time performers entering the palace, lifting one's head was unthinkable. 
Sanniang trembled so hard she barely knew what to do with her hands and feet. 
"She's thirteen—still just a little one." 
The Noble Consort said, her voice warm and gentle, pitched with perfect grace. Sanniang risked a glance upward. She saw a soft, dimpled smile—like spring light spilling over a garden in bloom. 

The Emperor wished to present a new composition, a song he wanted the troupe to sing for the Consort. 
It was said to be based on a village tune collected by wandering song‑gatherers—a melody about a young man longing for the one he loves, sleepless and restless. 
A man who ruled the world, able to bestow treasures beyond imagining—yet here he was, imitating the shy earnestness of a common boy, offering his heart a little awkwardly. 

Sanniang sang with exquisite care. She knew she wasn't bad—but she wasn't truly good either. 
In the Music Bureau, "not perfect" meant "wrong." 
As she waited for judgment, the words came: "Child, come here." 
She nearly stepped on her hem as she stumbled forward. 
The Noble Consort let out a soft laugh and placed a bright red fruit into her palm, saying she was delighted. 

Whatever the Emperor said afterward faded into a blur. It almost sounded as though he was asking what reward she desired— 
his voice low, authoritative, yet tinged with something gentler, almost coaxing. 
Around her, performers bowed, accepted their rewards, and withdrew. Spring was left to the Emperor and his beloved alone. 

Born into a family of musicians, chosen and welcomed into the Imperial Music Bureau—everything had unfolded as naturally as water flowing downhill. 
And as she stepped through the palace gates once more, Sanniang realized, quietly and to her own surprise: Perhaps she truly did love to sing.

zh:
【器用·一】

【剑】

古剑篇
郭震
君不见昆吾铁冶飞炎烟，红光紫气俱赫然。
良工锻炼凡几年，铸得宝剑名龙泉。
龙泉颜色如霜雪，良工咨嗟叹奇绝。
琉璃玉匣吐莲花，错镂金环映明月。
正逢天下无风尘，幸得周防君子身。
精光黯黯青蛇色，文章片片绿龟鳞。
非直结交游侠子，亦曾亲近英雄人。
何言中路遭弃捐，零落漂沦古狱边。
虽复尘埋无所用，犹能夜夜气冲天。

李都尉古剑
白居易
古剑寒黯黯，铸来几千秋。
白光纳日月，紫气排斗牛。
有客借一观，爱之不敢求。
湛然玉匣中，秋水澄不流。
至宝有本性，精刚无与俦。
可使寸寸折，不能绕指柔。
愿快直士心，将断佞臣头。
不愿报小怨，夜半刺私仇。
劝君慎所用，无作神兵羞。

【笔】

笔
李峤
握管门庭侧，含毫山水隈。
霜辉简上发，锦字梦中开。
鹦鹉摛文至，麒麟绝句来。
何当遇良史，左右振奇才。

紫毫笔
白居易
紫毫笔，尖如锥兮利如刀。
江南石上有老兔，吃竹饮泉生紫毫。
宣城之人采为笔，千万毛中拣一毫。
毫虽轻，功甚重。
管勒工名充岁贡，君兮臣兮勿轻用。
勿轻用，将何如？
愿赐东西府御史，愿颁左右台起居。
搦管趋入黄金阙，抽毫立在白玉除。
臣有奸邪正衙奏，君有动言直笔书。
起居郎，侍御史，尔知紫毫不易致。
每岁宣城进笔时，紫毫之价如金贵。
慎勿空将弹失仪，慎勿空将录制词。

【墨】

酬张司马赠墨
李白
上党碧松烟，夷陵丹砂末。
兰麝凝珍墨，精光乃堪掇。
黄头奴子双鸦鬟，锦囊养之怀袖间。
今日赠予兰亭去，兴来洒笔会稽山。

寓意诗五首·其一
白居易
豫樟生深山，七年而后知。
挺高二百尺，本末皆十围。
天子建明堂，此材独中规。
匠人执斤墨，采度将有期。
孟冬草木枯，烈火燎山陂。
疾风吹猛焰，从根烧到枝。
养材三十年，方成栋梁姿。
一朝为灰烬，柯叶无孑遗。
地虽生尔材，天不与尔时。
不如粪土英，犹有人掇之。
已矣勿重陈，重陈令人悲。
不悲焚烧苦，但悲采用迟。

【纸】

纸
李峤
妙迹蔡侯施，芳名左伯驰。
云飞锦绮落，花发缥红披。
舒卷随幽显，廉方合轨仪。
莫惊反掌字，当取葛洪规。
en:
【Implements · Part One】

【Sword】

Ode to an Ancient Sword
Guo Zhen
Have you not seen the Kunwu smelter's fiery smoke fly,
Where red light and purple aura both blaze high?
For years the master smith toiled with his art,
To forge the treasured sword named "Dragon Spring."
Its hue like frost and snow, pure and apart,
The master sighed, amazed at such a thing.
In a glass and jade case, lotus blooms it spits,
Gold rings engraved reflect the bright moon's light.
In times of peace, with no turmoil or strife,
It's fortunate to guard a noble's life.
Its dark gleam holds the hue of a green snake,
Its patterns like a turtle's emerald scale.
It not only befriended roving knights,
But also kept close company with heroes.
How can it be said it was cast aside midway?
Now lost and drifting by an ancient jail it lay.
Though buried in the dust, its use seems gone,
It still can pierce the sky each night at dawn.

Ancient Sword of Commandant Li
Bai Juyi
An ancient sword, cold and dim,
Forged how many autumns ago?
Its white light holds the sun and moon within,
Its purple aura pushes stars to and fro.
A guest borrowed it for a look,
Loving it but not daring to ask.
Serene within its jade case it lay,
Like autumn water, clear and still.
A treasure has its own true nature,
Pure and strong, none can compare.
It can be broken inch by inch,
But never made to bend and yield.
I wish to gladden the upright man's heart,
To sever the flattering minister's head.
I do not wish to settle petty grudges,
Nor stab for private vengeance in the night.
I urge you to be careful in its use,
Lest you bring shame upon this divine blade.

【Brush】

The Brush
Li Jiao
Holding the tube by the courtyard gate,
Moistening the tip by the mountain's bend.
Frosty radiance issues from the bamboo slip,
Brocade characters bloom within a dream.
The parrot brings its patterned prose,
The qilin arrives with perfect lines.
When will I meet a worthy historian,
To stir up wondrous talent left and right?

The Purple Hare Brush
Bai Juyi
The purple hare brush,
Its tip sharp as an awl, keen as a blade.
On southern rocks lives an old hare,
Eating bamboo, drinking spring water, growing purple fur.
The people of Xuancheng gather it for brushes,
Choosing one hair from ten thousand.
The hair is light, but the labor is great.
The tube bears the craftsman's name, sent as yearly tribute,
Oh ruler, oh minister, do not use it lightly.
Do not use it lightly, for what then?
I wish to grant it to the Censors of East and West,
I wish to bestow it upon the Diarists of Left and Right.
Grasping the tube, they hasten into the golden palace,
Drawing the tip, they stand by the white jade steps.
When ministers have wicked schemes, report them in the main court;
When the ruler has moving words, record them with a straight brush.
Diarist, Censor, you know the purple hair is hard to obtain.
Each year when Xuancheng presents its brushes,
The price of purple hair is as precious as gold.
Take care not to wield it idly to reprimand breaches of decorum,
Take care not to wield it idly to record empty phrases.

【Ink】

In Gratitude for Marshal Zhang's Gift of Ink
Li Bai
From Shangdang, green pine soot,
From Yiling, cinnabar dust.
Orchid and musk congeal into precious ink,
Its essence bright, worthy to be gathered.
A yellow-turbaned servant girl with twin raven locks,
Keeps it in a brocade pouch within her sleeve.
Today I give it for your journey to Orchid Pavilion,
When inspiration comes, to wield the brush on Kuaiji Mountain.

Five Allegorical Poems · The First
Bai Juyi
The camphor tree grows deep in the mountains,
Only known after seven years.
It towers two hundred feet high,
Its trunk and branches ten arm-spans round.
The Son of Heaven builds his Bright Hall,
This timber alone meets the measure.
The craftsman takes his axe and ink-line,
Planning to fell it in due time.
In early winter, grass and trees wither,
A fierce fire sweeps the mountain slope.
A swift wind fans the raging flames,
Burning from root to branch.
Thirty years nurtured to grow this timber,
Just formed into a pillar's shape.
In a single morning turned to ash,
Not a leaf or twig remains.
Though the earth gave birth to your material,
Heaven did not grant you the time.
Less than dung and soil, a hero,
Might still be gathered by someone.
Enough, speak no more of this,
Speaking again brings sorrow.
Not sorrow for the burning pain,
But sorrow for the felling, come too late.

【Paper】

Paper
Li Jiao
Marvelous traces, Marquis Cai bestowed,
A fine reputation, Zuo Bo spread afar.
Like clouds flying, brocade and damask fall,
Like flowers blooming, pale red unfolds.
Unfurling, rolling, following the hidden and revealed,
Upright and square, fitting rules and forms.
Do not startle at characters written in a palm's turn,
But take the rule of Ge Hong as your guide.
Yi Yu Yi Sheng
What could it be?
Xiaosheng

"When will you finally come to take me away?"

Yet before Bunbun was fully grown, the girl had to move away. It didn't understand her tears. To the kitten, they seemed like just another kind of game.
So when Bunbun finally grew up, it stayed behind in the village, waiting quietly, hoping the girl would return to take it home.

To $N,
Young friend, awake at last?
This old Daoist divined that you must have slept like the dead during these days of rest.

Rest is over, young friend. Time to rise and train.

zh:
直到那天，镇外来了个游侠。
那游侠在蒙学馆里转悠，周怀民正好在里面读书，游侠拦住他，问：“小先生，这镇上哪儿有好玩的地方？”
周怀民放下书说：“涌泉镇七十二泉，各有典故。你要听哪一泉的故事？”
游侠说：“都听都听！”
周怀民一愣。他没想到真有人愿意听。他清了清嗓子，从“爆流泉”的来历讲到“珍珠泉”的传说，又讲到四海生平泉为什么被称为天下第一泉。游侠听得津津有味，时不时还问几句。周怀民越讲越起劲，干脆把书放在石阶上，比划着手势说。
讲完了，游侠竖起大拇指说：“小先生真厉害！”
周怀民脸一红，说：“闻道有先后，术业有专攻，我不过是在这镇上多住了几年，不足挂齿。”
那天之后，游侠在镇上盘桓了几日，每日都来找周怀民。周怀民带着游侠去看泉、看风筝坊、看金盆镖行门口的大金盆。游侠给他讲江湖上的事，讲走过哪些路、见过哪些人。周怀民听得眼睛发亮，嘴上却说：“这些都是旁门左道，你日后还是要多读书，把心思放在正业上。”
游侠笑了，说：“那你为什么听得这么认真？”
周怀民不说话了。他别过脸，假装在看远处的风筝。过了一会儿，他回过头，正色道：“这叫敏而好学，不耻下问，你再多讲讲江湖上的事吧！”
en:
That was, until the day a wanderer came to town.
The traveler was strolling around Primary Hall when they spotted Zhou Huaimin reading inside. Stopping in their tracks, the traveler asked, "Say, Little Master, where's the fun to be had around here?"
Zhou Huaimin set his book aside. "Wellspring Town has seventy-two springs, and every single one has a history. Which one's story do you want to hear?"
"All of them!" the wanderer replied eagerly.
Zhou Huaimin blinked. He genuinely hadn't expected anyone to actually want to listen. Clearing his throat, he started with the origins of the Bursting Torrent Spring, moved on to the legend of the Pearl Spring, and finally explained why the Springs of Universal Peace were known as the greatest in the world. The traveler listened intently, chiming in with the occasional question. Caught up in the excitement, the boy completely abandoned his scroll on the stone steps, gesturing wildly as he talked.
When he finally finished, the wanderer gave him a thumbs-up. "You really know your stuff, Little Master!"
Zhou Huaimin's face flushed bright red. "Mastery comes to some earlier than others, and every trade has its focus," he recited modestly. "I have simply lived here a few years longer than you. It is nothing worth mentioning."
The wanderer ended up staying in town for a few more days, seeking out the boy every single afternoon. Zhou Huaimin played the tour guide, showing off the local springs, the kite workshop, and the massive golden basin outside the Golden Basin Escort Agency. In exchange, the wanderer shared tales of the jianghu, the dusty roads they had traveled, and the eccentric characters they had met along the way. Zhou Huaimin's eyes practically sparkled as he listened, even though he couldn't resist a bit of lecturing. "These are unorthodox paths," he scolded lightly. "You really ought to read more and focus your mind on proper pursuits."
The wanderer just laughed. "Then why are you listening so closely?"
Zhou Huaimin clammed up. He quickly looked away, pretending to be utterly fascinated by a kite in the distance. After a long moment, he turned back, put on a completely straight face, and declared, "The classics say an earnest scholar is never ashamed to ask questions of anyone. Now, tell me more about the jianghu!"

有人路过没忍住，插嘴指出错误，没被责怪，反而被那位长老请进课堂里，拉去一起听课、讨论。
怪，哪有这样的学堂，又哪有这样的先生？
en:
Something strange has been going on among the refugees of Bujian Mountains lately.
A kindly Elder has come up the mountain and started teaching classes in the shacks. But instead of lessons in scholarship or mechanics, he's been teaching the disciples how to use a big stove, how to start a fire, and how to cook porridge.
One passerby couldn't help interrupting to point out a mistake. Far from scolding him, the Elder invited him right into the lesson to listen in and join the discussion.
Strange, isn't it? What kind of school teaches like that, and what kind of teacher welcomes interruptions?

zh:
沈玉这半生，听见的大多都不是自己爱听的话，听多了，她便不爱听人说话。
这事不难，毕竟他们还教了她旁的东西，教了她如何笑，如何哭，如何笑得好看，在席上体面，如何笑得够久，久到让别人体面；如何哭得动人，用帕子碰着眼角，眼泪不许多掉一滴，也不许少掉一滴。
因此，她在不听人话的时候，也依旧是那副笑模样，于是旁人都说，沈玉顶了天的听话。

但她不总是这样听话的。
六岁那年，去爹的书房里送吃食，她便拿起一本策论，一句一句读起来，有些字她不认识，她便只念半边，笑眯眯地翻页，直到爹沉着脸出来，她不明所以，被爹狠狠训斥了一顿。
那时候她知道，一个人读不该读的书，是要挨打的。

八岁那年，沈玉偷溜出府，瞧着满街上的新鲜物件，跑来跑去，看来看去，第二日，爹将她叫到厅堂。
沈侍御史的旁边有两个人，一个是个凶巴巴的婆婆，一个是昨日跟着她出门的小厮，她从此日日跟着那位婆婆学哭、学笑、学走路、学不可多吃几口。
那时候她知道，一个人走不能走的路，是要挨打的。

十二岁那年，她偶尔在出门赏花之时，看见水池面上倒映的那张笑脸，她看了一会儿，捡起一颗石子掷过去，那影子便一圈圈泛开，脸上的笑变得模糊，后来她被打了手板，沈侍御史问她为何贪玩，她没有说，是那张脸上的笑，看起来假得吓人，她不喜欢。
这时候，她已经知道，一个人说不能说的话，是要挨打的。

“笼中雀又如何，掀了屋顶，不便是龙中雀嘛，龙中雀，何处去不得。”
他们始终不知道，他们对沈玉说了千百句话，为何最后比不过别人的一句话。
可是——
一个人是不会仅仅被一句话打动的，除非这本就是一句她想要说的话。
en:
Most of what Shen Yu heard in her life were things she never wanted to hear. Eventually, she stopped wanting to hear anything at all.

It wasn't hard. After all, they'd taught her other things. How to smile, how to cry. How to smile a beautiful, decorous smile at a banquet, how to keep smiling long enough to let others save face. How to cry just right, dabbing the corners of her eyes with a handkerchief, not a tear too many, not a tear too few.

So even when she stopped listening, she still wore that same practiced smile. So everyone said that Shen Yu was the most obedient girl in the world.

But she hadn't always been so obedient.

When she was six, she brought food to her father's study. She picked up a policy treatise and read it aloud line by line. Some characters she didn't know, so she read only half of them, flipping pages with a cheerful grin. When her father stormed out, face scowling, she didn't understand. And she got scolded by her father.

She learned that reading what you're not supposed to read will earn you punishment.

When she was eight, she slipped out of the estate for the first time. The streets were full of wonders she had never seen before, so many things to see. The next day, her father summoned her. Beside him stood two figures: a sharp-tongued grannie, and the pageboy who had followed her out yesterday.

From then on, she studied under that grannie every day. How to cry, how to smile, how to walk, how not to eat more than a few bites.

She learned that walking where you're not supposed to walk will earn you a punishment.

When she was twelve, while out admiring flowers, she glimpsed her reflection in a pond. She stared at the smiling face in the water. Then she picked up a stone and tossed it in. Ripples blurred the smile into something eerie.

Later, she was caned on the palms. Imperial Censor Shen asked her reason for being playful. She didn't answer. She didn't tell them that her smile had looked so fake it frightened her. She hadn't liked it.

Because by then, she already knew that saying what you're not supposed to say will earn you a punishment.

"A caged bird," someone once said, "just take the roof off, and it becomes a dragon. And a dragon can fly wherever it wants."

They never understood. After telling Shen Yu a thousand things, how could they be undone by just a single sentence from someone else?

But then again, a person is never truly moved by a single sentence. Unless it's something she's always wanted to say herself.

zh: 鱼袋。其制自唐始，盖以为符契也。其始曰鱼符，左一右一，左者进内，右者随身，刻官姓名，出入合之。因盛以袋，故曰鱼袋。宋因之，其制以金银饰为鱼形，公服则繋于带而垂于后，以明贵贱，非复如唐之符契也。
en: The fish-emblem pouch began in the Tang as a practical badge of office and evolved into a clear mark of rank. In the Tang system, officials carried paired "fish tokens," one left at the gate, one carried on the person, both engraved with the holder's name and matched on entry; these tokens were kept in a pouch, hence the name. By the Song, the token practice fell away. Instead, fish-shaped ornaments in gold or silver were worn on the belt (usually hanging at the back) and became the direct, visible sign of an official's status, while the pouch itself also served to hold small personal items.

zh:
手手是只惯会讨人欢心的猫。
它一见到人，就主动躺倒在地，喵喵喵叫个不停、蹭个不停。它既不咬人，也从不突然发狠，哪个路过的人能忍住不去一摸再摸呢？
摸这样一只可爱的猫，成了许多人血路苦旅中的唯一一点温存。
似乎只有在摸它头的时候，才能够短暂地忘掉一些仇恨、疼痛和目标。
软软的、糯糯的——此刻仿佛是只有猫存在的世界。
手手真是只好猫！
如果它能不趁旅人松懈之时，叼走他们身上的干粮和碎钱，就更好了。
en:
Pawsie is a master of winning hearts.
The moment it spots someone, it flops onto its side, purring and rubbing against their legs without pause. It never bites, never scratches. Who could resist?
For weary travelers on blood-soaked journeys, petting this soft little creature offers a rare moment of warmth. 
As hands stroke through its fur, grudges fade, pain dulls, even missions feel distant. The world becomes simple: just soft paws, gentle purrs, and a fleeting peace.
Pawsie truly is a wonderful cat... if only it didn't swipe travelers' food and coins the second they let their guard down.

【国风·唐风】

蟋蟀

蟋蟀在堂，岁聿其莫。今我不乐，日月其除。无已大康，职思其居。好乐无荒，良士瞿瞿。
蟋蟀在堂，岁聿其逝。今我不乐，日月其迈。无已大康，职思其外。好乐无荒，良士蹶蹶。
蟋蟀在堂，役车其休。今我不乐，日月其慆。无已大康，职思其忧。好乐无荒，良士休休。

山有枢

山有枢，隰有榆。子有衣裳，弗曳弗娄。子有车马，弗驰弗驱。宛其死矣，他人是愉。
山有栲，隰有杽。子在廷内，弗洒弗埽。子有钟鼓，弗鼓弗考。宛其死矣，他人是保。
山有漆，隰有栗。子有酒食，何不日鼓瑟？且以喜乐，且以永日。宛其死矣，他人入室。

扬之水

扬之水，白石凿凿。素衣朱襮，从子于沃。既见君子，云何不乐？
扬之水，白石皓皓。素衣朱绣，从子于鹄。既见君子，云何其忧？
扬之水，白石粼粼。我闻有命，不敢以告人。
……
en:
【Classic of Poetry - Odes of Tang】

The Cricket

The cricket chirps in the hall, the year draws near its close. If I do not enjoy myself now, the sun and moon will pass me by. But do not indulge in excessive pleasure; remember your duties and your place. Enjoyment without neglect—this is how the noble man is ever vigilant.
The cricket chirps in the hall, the year is slipping away. If I do not enjoy myself now, the sun and moon will march on. But do not indulge in excessive pleasure; remember your duties beyond. Enjoyment without neglect—this is how the noble man is ever diligent.
The cricket chirps in the hall, the carts of labor come to rest. If I do not enjoy myself now, the sun and moon will swiftly flee. But do not indulge in excessive pleasure; remember your duties and your cares. Enjoyment without neglect—this is how the noble man finds contentment.

The Mountain Has the Thorn-Elm

On the mountain grows the thorn-elm, in the lowland grows the elm. You have robes and garments, yet you do not wear or trail them. You have carriages and horses, yet you do not drive or gallop them. When you lie dead, others will take delight in them.
On the mountain grows the evergreen chinquapin, in the lowland grows the tree of heaven. You have halls and chambers, yet you do not sprinkle or sweep them. You have bells and drums, yet you do not beat or strike them. When you lie dead, others will preserve them.
On the mountain grows the lacquer tree, in the lowland grows the chestnut tree. You have wine and food, why not daily play the zither? Let us be merry and joyful, let us make the long day last. When you lie dead, others will enter your chamber.

The Flowing Waters

The flowing waters, the white stones so clear. In plain robes with red collar, I follow you to Wo. Having seen my lord, how can I not be glad?
The flowing waters, the white stones so bright. In plain robes with red embroidery, I follow you to Hu. Having seen my lord, how can there be any sorrow?
The flowing waters, the white stones so gleaming. I have heard the command, but dare not tell anyone.
…

zh:
猫还是小猫时，遇到个青年，脸是好的，心是软的，人却是傻的。它不过在路边躺上一躺，那青年就大惊小怪——可是受伤？可是饿了？
青年的怀抱很软，猫猫没挣扎。但青年竟忘了给它起名，果真是个傻的！
后来猫猫被青年带给一个姑娘，姑娘什么都很会养，猫猫很满意这个姑娘。姑娘家的小崽子整天小白小白的叫，猫猫从此就叫小白。
后来的后来，那人不再来了，姑娘也不见了。猫猫的尾巴被火燎得很疼，它忍着疼跑啊跑，跑了很久，抬头时，却又回到了原地。
猫猫没有眼泪，伸长脖子看清是家后，猫猫只想回到小窝，睡个长长的觉。
梦里三个主人都在，猫还是小猫。
en:
When it was just a kitten, Xiaobai met a young man—handsome, soft-hearted, but a little clueless. It simply lay by the roadside, and he was instantly worried: "Are you hurt? Are you hungry?" 
His arms were gentle and warm, so it didn't struggle. But he forgot the one important thing—giving it a name. Truly, a foolish man! 
Later, he brought Xiaobai to a girl who knew how to care for animals, and Xiaobai liked her right away. The little one in the girl's house called it "Xiaobai," and the name stuck. 
But soon after, the man stopped coming, and the girl disappeared too. Xiaobai's tail was burned by fire, yet it ran on, despite the pain. When it finally looked up, it was back where it started. 
Cats don't shed tears, but seeing home again, Xiaobai only wanted to curl up in her nest and sleep long and deep. 
In its dreams, all three owners were there—and she was still a kitten.

田英者，清河人也。少时贫寒，而无所知名。求学文津馆，后事道济。道济甚尊之。
及世宗伐辽，辽主遣其舅使于唐，道济谓田英曰：“此时不可失，不求何愚!”英曰：“辽使可杀也。唐虽有绣金之卫，而无将兵之力。以此威慑之，无如我何？”道济赞曰：“非以行间，乃谋国事，君知我也”。
后唐人夜宴辽使于清风驿，酒酣，起更衣，久不至，失其首也。唐主使绣金楼捕田英，未得。自是辽与唐绝。亦无复有人见田英矣。
en:
Tian Ying was a native of Qinghe. In his youth, he lived in poverty and remained unknown. He studied at the Inkbound Order before serving under Daoji, who held him in high esteem. 
When Emperor Shizong launched a campaign against the Liao Dynasty, the Liao ruler sent his uncle as an envoy to the Southern Tang. Daoji said to Tian Ying, "This opportunity must not be missed—how foolish to let it slip!" Tian Ying replied, "The Liao envoy can be assassinated. Although the Southern Tang has the Aureate Guards, they lack the power to command troops. By intimidating them in this way, what can they do to us?" Daoji praised him, saying, "This is not about espionage but state affairs. You understand my intentions." 
Later, the Southern Tang hosted a night banquet for the Liao envoy at Qingfeng Post . When the envoy withdrew to relieve himself after drinking heavily, he did not return for a long time—and was found decapitated. The Southern Tang ruler ordered the Aureate Pavilion to arrest Tian Ying, but he evaded capture. From then on, diplomatic relations between Liao and Southern Tang were severed, and Tian Ying was never seen again.

榫卯结构方便生产、安装与拆卸，受力稳固，且能承受一定程度的形变，对地震灾害亦有一定抗性。
en:
The art of mortise and tenon joins wood without nails or glue. The tenon is the protruding piece, and the mortise is the matching slot.
Widely used in ancient Chinese buildings, these joints took many forms as early as the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, including shoulder joints, dovetails, through-tenons, and hooked joints. They are easy to produce, assemble, dismantle, and repair, while remaining stable under load and resilient against deformation, including during earthquakes.

出尘之心，与他为天下先的入世之心，本无高下可分。麦陵野人虽未如愿，但也以忘年友人之身，授胡昌翼以护身之技、存身之术。
